literature.headline_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期基孔肯雅病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 自 2013 年引入美洲以来,CHIKV 的全球传播率一直很高,2025 年报告了超过 180,000 例确诊病例。 [10.1007/978-1-0716-5496-5_1]
近期对基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)复制酶核心的结构研究显示,病毒的RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶nsP4与nsP1和nsP2均相互作用,并预测其会与病毒RNA结合。 [10.1128/mbio.01638-26]
恢复期个体的ADCC反应与血浆抗CHIKV IgG和IgG3抗体水平呈正相关(IgG: r = 0.4503,IgG3: r = 0.4583,每个p值均<0.01)。在慢性基孔肯雅病毒关节炎患者中观察到ADCC反应逐渐下降,而在恢复期个体中则观察到ADCC反应持续存在,持续时间从感染后3个月到18年不等。 [10.1016/j.virol.2026.111076]
最常见的症状是关节痛(n = 326)和发热(n = 317)。未报告死亡病例。在263个Aedes albopictus蚊虫池中,检测到39个(14.8%)含有CHIKV RNA,从而确认了本地传播的基孔肯雅病毒。 [10.2807/1560-7917.es.2026.31.36.2500962]
该综述强调了甲型病毒对全球公共卫生的显著影响,包括新暴发的风险、高传播率以及导致严重残疾或潜在致命的临床表现。它确定了与甲型病毒感染相关的关键致病途径和分子机制。 [10.17605/osf.io/xzfht]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: HLA-A02 was enriched among pCHIKV-CIJD patients (35.9% vs. 14.8%; OR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.21-9.21, p = 0.012), and the B62 supertype was also more frequent in the chronic group (15.6% vs. 3.7%; OR = 4.76, 95% CI: 0.95-46.73, p = 0.037). [10.1016/j.humimm.2026.112067]
Since its introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence of CHIKV remains high, with over 180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. [10.1007/978-1-0716-5496-5_1]

In univariable analysis, arthralgia (OR = 5.84, 95% CI 5.39-6.33) and fever (OR = 5.85, 95% CI 5.29-6.46) were most positively associated with Chikungunya. The macro-AUC values ranged from 0.89 to 0.90 for all models in the multiclass analysis. [10.1007/s15010-026-02963-z]

Recent structural studies of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) replicase core revealed that the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase nsP4 interacts with both nsP1 and nsP2 and is predicted to engage viral RNA. [10.1128/mbio.01638-26]

Recovered individuals showed a positive correlation between ADCC response and plasma anti-CHIKV IgG and IgG3 antibody levels (IgG: r = 0.4503, IgG3: r = 0.4583, p-value < 0.01 for each). [10.1016/j.virol.2026.111076]

papers.title: HLA polymorphisms potentially associated with susceptibility to chronic post-chikungunya inflammatory joint disease: an exploratory study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: A substantial proportion of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV)-infected patients progress to post-Chikungunya chronic inflammatory joint disease (pCHIKV-CIJD), yet host genetic determinants of this outcome remain poorly understood. HLA polymorphisms are established risk factors for inflammatory arthropathies, but their role in CHIKV chronification has not been investigated. OBJECTIVES: To explore associations between HLA alleles and progression to pCHIKV-CIJD in a Brazilian cohort. STUDY DESIGN: We performed in silico HLA typing from whole-blood RNA-seq data of 59 CHIKV-infected patients (32 pCHIKV-CIJD and 27 non-pCHIKV-CIJD) using HLAminer. We compared allelic frequencies at two-digit resolution using Fisher's exact test with Bonferroni correction. Additional analyses included supertype classification, heterozygosity scoring, KIR ligand grouping, and logistic regression adjusted for sex, age, and race. RESULTS: HLA-A02 was enriched among pCHIKV-CIJD patients (35.9% vs. 14.8%; OR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.21-9.21, p = 0.012), remaining nominally significant after covariate adjustment (adjusted OR = 3.57, 95% CI: 1.09-11.73, p = 0.036). The B62 supertype was also more frequent in the chronic group (15.6% vs. 3.7%; OR = 4.76, 95% CI: 0.95-46.73, p = 0.037). Chronic patients showed lower HLA heterozygosity (p = 0.043). However, no association survived the Bonferroni correction. CONCLUSIONS: Our data support a potential association between HLA-A02 carriage and an increased risk of pCHIKV-CIJD. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, independent cohorts.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study included 59 CHIKV-infected patients (32 pCHIKV-CIJD and 27 non-pCHIKV-CIJD) from Brazil, using in silico HLA typing from whole-blood RNA-seq data.
analysis.methods: HLA typing was performed using HLAminer, with additional analyses including supertype classification, heterozygosity scoring, KIR ligand grouping, and logistic regression adjusted for sex, age, and race.
analysis.main_results: HLA-A02 was enriched among pCHIKV-CIJD patients (35.9% vs. 14.8%; OR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.21-9.21, p = 0.012), and the B62 supertype was also more frequent in the chronic group (15.6% vs. 3.7%; OR = 4.76, 95% CI: 0.95-46.73, p = 0.037). analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The data support a potential association between HLA-A02 carriage and an increased risk of pCHIKV-CIJD, which is hypothesis-generating and requires validation in larger, independent cohorts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HLA-A02 may be a risk factor for chronic post-Chikungunya inflammatory joint disease, which could inform future studies and potentially influence surveillance and diagnosis.

analysis.summary_en: This study explored the association between HLA alleles and chronic post-Chikungunya inflammatory joint disease in a Brazilian cohort. HLA-A02 was found to be enriched in pCHIKV-CIJD patients, but the findings require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title_zh: HLA多态性与慢性基孔肯雅热炎症性关节病易感性潜在关联:一项探索性研究
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: A substantial proportion of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV)-infected patients progress to post-Chikungunya chronic inflammatory joint disease (pCHIKV-CIJD), yet host genetic determinants of this outcome remain poorly understood. HLA polymorphisms are established risk factors for inflammatory arthropathies, but their role in CHIKV chronification has not been investigated. OBJECTIVES: To explore associations between HLA alleles and progression to pCHIKV-CIJD in a Brazilian cohort. STUDY DESIGN: We performed in silico HLA typing from whole-blood RNA-seq data of 59 CHIKV-infected patients (32 pCHIKV-CIJD and 27 non-pCHIKV-CIJD) using HLAminer. We compared allelic frequencies at two-digit resolution using Fisher's exact test with Bonferroni correction. Additional analyses included supertype classification, heterozygosity scoring, KIR ligand grouping, and logistic regression adjusted for sex, age, and race. RESULTS: HLA-A02 was enriched among pCHIKV-CIJD patients (35.9% vs. 14.8%; OR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.21-9.21, p = 0.012), remaining nominally significant after covariate adjustment (adjusted OR = 3.57, 95% CI: 1.09-11.73, p = 0.036). The B62 supertype was also more frequent in the chronic group (15.6% vs. 3.7%; OR = 4.76, 95% CI: 0.95-46.73, p = 0.037). Chronic patients showed lower HLA heterozygosity (p = 0.043). However, no association survived the Bonferroni correction. CONCLUSIONS: Our data support a potential association between HLA-A02 carriage and an increased risk of pCHIKV-CIJD. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger, independent cohorts.

papers.title: Targeting conserved interaction surfaces of alphavirus nsP4 supports the rational design of live-attenuated vaccine candidates.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Alphaviruses are emerging arboviruses that pose a growing threat to global public health; however, effective interventions remain limited. Recent structural studies of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) replicase core revealed that the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase nsP4 interacts with both nsP1 and nsP2 and is predicted to engage viral RNA. The conservation and multifunctionality of nsP4 make it a challenging but promising target for rational attenuation. Here, we evaluated 58 structure-guided mutations in nsP4 predicted to disrupt interactions with nsP1, nsP2, or viral RNA using a trans-replicase system. Sixteen selected mutations were further analyzed in a CHIKV-o'nyong-nyong virus chimera and Semliki Forest virus (SFV). Most mutants were viable but showed varying degrees of attenuation in mammalian and mosquito cells. Viruses carrying mutations in predicted RNA-interaction sites frequently acquired pseudoreversions and/or second-site compensatory changes, whereas those harboring mutations affecting nsP1 or nsP2 interfaces were more genetically stable. Three substitutions representing defects in nsP1 interaction (F164A), predicted RNA interaction (K174S), and nsP2 interaction (D393A) were further characterized in authentic CHIKV and displayed attenuation consistent with that observed in SFV. In vivo, all three variants showed reduced pathogenicity in the SFV mouse model, with F164A being avirulent, immunogenic, and conferring complete protection against lethal challenge. In a CHIKV mouse model, these mutations attenuated disease and reduced serum virus titers and inflammatory cell infiltration. Together, these findings provide a molecular framework for the rational design of live-attenuated alphavirus vaccine candidates and support broader evaluation of nsP4-based attenuation. IMPORTANCE: Alphaviruses are an increasing global health concern, with hundreds of thousands of chikungunya cases reported worldwide in 2025; however, vaccine options remain limited, and no specific antiviral treatment is available. Recent structural studies have revealed conserved functional interfaces in the viral RNA polymerase nsP4, but their value for attenuation had not been systematically explored. Here, using structure-guided mutagenesis, validation in multiple viral systems, and in vivo analysis, we show that selected nsP4 mutations can strongly attenuate replication and pathogenicity while preserving immunogenicity. These findings identify conserved nsP4 interfaces as a shared vulnerability of alphaviruses and provide a molecular framework for the rational design of broadly applicable live-attenuated vaccines while also highlighting nsP4 as a functionally constrained target relevant to antiviral development.

papers.title_zh: 靶向阿尔法病毒nsP4保守相互作用表面支持理性的活减毒疫苗候选疫苗设计。
papers.source_body_en: UNLABELLED: Alphaviruses are emerging arboviruses that pose a growing threat to global public health; however, effective interventions remain limited. Recent structural studies of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) replicase core revealed that the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase nsP4 interacts with both nsP1 and nsP2 and is predicted to engage viral RNA. The conservation and multifunctionality of nsP4 make it a challenging but promising target for rational attenuation. Here, we evaluated 58 structure-guided mutations in nsP4 predicted to disrupt interactions with nsP1, nsP2, or viral RNA using a trans-replicase system. Sixteen selected mutations were further analyzed in a CHIKV-o'nyong-nyong virus chimera and Semliki Forest virus (SFV). Most mutants were viable but showed varying degrees of attenuation in mammalian and mosquito cells. Viruses carrying mutations in predicted RNA-interaction sites frequently acquired pseudoreversions and/or second-site compensatory changes, whereas those harboring mutations affecting nsP1 or nsP2 interfaces were more genetically stable. Three substitutions representing defects in nsP1 interaction (F164A), predicted RNA interaction (K174S), and nsP2 interaction (D393A) were further characterized in authentic CHIKV and displayed attenuation consistent with that observed in SFV. In vivo, all three variants showed reduced pathogenicity in the SFV mouse model, with F164A being avirulent, immunogenic, and conferring complete protection against lethal challenge. In a CHIKV mouse model, these mutations attenuated disease and reduced serum virus titers and inflammatory cell infiltration. Together, these findings provide a molecular framework for the rational design of live-attenuated alphavirus vaccine candidates and support broader evaluation of nsP4-based attenuation. IMPORTANCE: Alphaviruses are an increasing global health concern, with hundreds of thousands of chikungunya cases reported worldwide in 2025; however, vaccine options remain limited, and no specific antiviral treatment is available. Recent structural studies have revealed conserved functional interfaces in the viral RNA polymerase nsP4, but their value for attenuation had not been systematically explored. Here, using structure-guided mutagenesis, validation in multiple viral systems, and in vivo analysis, we show that selected nsP4 mutations can strongly attenuate replication and pathogenicity while preserving immunogenicity. These findings identify conserved nsP4 interfaces as a shared vulnerability of alphaviruses and provide a molecular framework for the rational design of broadly applicable live-attenuated vaccines while also highlighting nsP4 as a functionally constrained target relevant to antiviral development.
papers.abstract_zh: UNLABELLED:阿尔法病毒是新兴的虫媒病毒,对全球公共卫生构成了日益严重的威胁;然而,有效的干预措施仍然有限。最近对基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)复制酶核心结构的研究表明,病毒RNA依赖的RNA聚合酶nsP4与nsP1和nsP2相互作用,并预测其与病毒RNA结合。nsP4的高度保守性和多功能性使其成为一种具有挑战性但有前景的理性减毒靶标。在此,我们使用跨复制系统评估了58种结构指导的突变,这些突变体预测可以破坏与nsP1、nsP2或病毒RNA的相互作用。经过进一步分析,16种选定的突变在CHIKV-o'nyong-nyong病毒嵌合体和塞米里森林病毒(SFV)中进行了研究。大多数突变体在哺乳动物和蚊子细胞中存活,但表现出不同程度的减毒。携带突变的病毒在预测的RNA结合位点经常获得假回复突变和/或第二位点补偿性变化,而那些影响nsP1或nsP2界面的突变体则表现出更高的遗传稳定性。三种代表nsP1相互作用缺陷(F164A)、预测RNA相互作用(K174S)和nsP2相互作用(D393A)的突变体在真实的CHIKV中进一步表征,其减毒程度与SFV中观察到的一致。体内研究中,所有三种变体在SFV小鼠模型中显示出降低的致病性,F164A无毒、免疫原性,并能完全保护免受致命挑战。在CHIKV小鼠模型中,这些突变减缓了疾病进程,降低了血清病毒滴度和炎症细胞浸润。这些发现为理性设计广泛适用的减毒活阿尔法病毒疫苗候选疫苗提供了分子框架,并支持对基于nsP4的减毒进行更广泛的评估。重要性:阿尔法病毒是日益严重的全球公共卫生问题,2025年全球报告了数十万例基孔肯雅热病例;然而,疫苗选项仍然有限,目前没有特定的抗病毒药物 治疗可用。最近的结构研究表明,病毒RNA聚合酶nsP4中存在保守的功能界面,但它们的价值尚未系统地进行探索。在此,我们使用结构指导的突变体,通过多种病毒系统验证和体内分析,表明选定的nsP4 突变可以强烈减缓复制和致病性,同时保留免疫原性。这些发现确定了保守的nsP4界面作为阿尔法病毒的共同脆弱性,并为广泛适用的减毒活阿尔法病毒疫苗的理性设计提供了分子框架,同时也突显了nsP4作为与抗病毒药物开发相关的功能受限靶标的重要性。

papers.title: A machine learning approach for differential classification of chikungunya virus: an explainable AI study based on surveillance data.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Mosquito-borne viral diseases such as chikungunya usually present similar clinical symptoms, which makes them hard to differentiate without laboratory confirmatory tests. Therefore, this work retrospectively developed interpretable machine learning models to improve the classification of chikungunya using routinely collected data. METHODS: Brazilian surveillance data, with 18,127 records, were analyzed, and eight different machine learning algorithms were trained and five-fold cross-validated. In addition, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and permutation feature importance described model behavior. RESULTS: In univariable analysis, arthralgia (OR = 5.84, 95% CI 5.39-6.33) and fever (OR = 5.85, 95% CI 5.29-6.46) were most positively associated with Chikungunya. The macro-AUC values ranged from 0.89 to 0.90 for all models in the multiclass analysis. The Chikungunya-versus-Non-Chikungunya task demonstrated moderate discrimination. The Chikungunya-versus-Dengue scenario produced the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.97 in most models. CONCLUSION: The explainability mechanism characterized how fitted models utilized available clinical and demographic predictors, with acute symptom variables contributing prominently to predictions. The results demonstrate the potential of using an interpretable model-assisted approach for arboviral classification. Importantly, prospective, temporal, and external geographic validation, with harmonized data, are required before clinical decision-support or point-of-care implementation can be considered.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to improve the classification of chikungunya virus using machine learning models based on surveillance data. The researchers developed interpretable models using Brazilian data with 18,127 records, training eight algorithms and employing SHAP and permutation feature importance for model behavior analysis. The results showed that arthralgia and fever were strongly associated with chikungunya, with macro-AUC values ranging from 0.89 to 0.90 in multiclass analysis. The Chikungunya-versus-Dengue scenario had the highest performance, achieving an AUC of 0.97. The models' explainability highlighted the importance of acute symptom variables in predictions. The study suggests that interpretable machine learning could aid in arboviral classification, though further validation is needed for clinical use. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the retrospective design and the need for external validation.

papers.source_body_en: PURPOSE: Mosquito-borne viral diseases such as chikungunya usually present similar clinical symptoms, which makes them hard to differentiate without laboratory confirmatory tests. Therefore, this work retrospectively developed interpretable machine learning models to improve the classification of chikungunya using routinely collected data. METHODS: Brazilian surveillance data, with 18,127 records, were analyzed, and eight different machine learning algorithms were trained and five-fold cross-validated. In addition, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and permutation feature importance described model behavior. RESULTS: In univariable analysis, arthralgia (OR = 5.84, 95% CI 5.39-6.33) and fever (OR = 5.85, 95% CI 5.29-6.46) were most positively associated with Chikungunya. The macro-AUC values ranged from 0.89 to 0.90 for all models in the multiclass analysis. The Chikungunya-versus-Non-Chikungunya task demonstrated moderate discrimination. The Chikungunya-versus-Dengue scenario produced the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.97 in most models. CONCLUSION: The explainability mechanism characterized how fitted models utilized available clinical and demographic predictors, with acute symptom variables contributing prominently to predictions. The results demonstrate the potential of using an interpretable model-assisted approach for arboviral classification. Importantly, prospective, temporal, and external geographic validation, with harmonized data, are required before clinical decision-support or point-of-care implementation can be considered.

papers.title: Natural-killer-cell-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity response in acute and recovery phases of chikungunya.
papers.abstract: Antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) mediated by natural killer (NK) cells is well documented in the clearance of various viral infections. Beyond direct virus neutralization, virus-specific antibodies confer protection through effector functions involving ADCC. NK cells have been identified as key contributors in chikungunya pathogenesis. This study evaluates NK cell-mediated ADCC involvement in chikungunya by assessing chikungunya virus (CHIKV)-specific ADCC responses in 56 acute, 56 prolonged, and 44 chronic chikungunya arthritis patients, 23 recovered individuals, and 50 healthy controls. A flow-cytometry-based antibody-dependent heterologous NK cell activation assay was employed, utilizing CD107a and IFN-γ as surrogate markers. Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney test, binary data were analyzed by Fisher's exact test, and correlations between ADCC response, CHIKV viral loads, total anti-CHIKV IgG, and IgG3 antibody levels were assessed by Spearman rank correlation. P values < 0.05 were considered significant. Persistence of ADCC response was observed in recovered individuals for durations ranging from 3 months to 18 years post-infection, while a progressive decline was noted in patients with chronic chikungunya arthritis. An inverse association between ADCC response and viral load was observed in a subset of acute patients. Recovered individuals demonstrated a positive correlation between ADCC response and plasma anti-CHIKV IgG and IgG3 antibody levels (IgG: r = 0.4503, IgG3: r = 0.4583, p-value < 0.01 for each). Collectively, these findings establish the role of NK cell-mediated ADCC response in chikungunya infection and provide a foundation for future antibody-based therapeutics for chikungunya, particularly utilizing IgG3 antibodies with functional ADCC capacity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the role of natural killer (NK) cell-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) in chikungunya infection, building on the established understanding that ADCC contributes to viral clearance in various infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study assessed chikungunya virus (CHIKV)-specific ADCC responses in 56 acute, 56 prolonged, and 44 chronic chikungunya arthritis patients, 23 recovered individuals, and 50 healthy controls to understand the dynamics of NK cell activity across different phases of infection.
analysis.methods: A flow-cytometry-based antibody-dependent heterologous NK cell activation assay was used, with CD107a and IFN-γ as surrogate markers. Statistical comparisons were made using the Mann-Whitney test, Fisher's exact test for binary data, and Spearman rank correlation for assessing relationships between ADCC response and antibody levels.
analysis.main_results: Recovered individuals showed a positive correlation between ADCC response and plasma anti-CHIKV IgG and IgG3 antibody levels (IgG: r = 0.4503, IgG3: r = 0.4583, p-value < 0.01 for each). A progressive decline in ADCC response was noted in patients with chronic chikungunya arthritis, while persistence was observed in recovered individuals for durations ranging from 3 months to 18 years post-infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish the role of NK cell-mediated ADCC in chikungunya infection and highlight the potential of IgG3 antibodies for antibody-based therapeutics, particularly in the context of long-term immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the immune mechanisms of chikungunya and may inform the development of antibody-based treatments and strategies for monitoring immune responses in infected individuals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's generalizability may be limited by its observational nature and the potential for confounding factors, though the evidence is supported by statistical analyses and is considered moderate in strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of natural killer (NK) cell-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) in chikungunya infection across different phases. It evaluates ADCC responses in acute, prolonged, and chronic chikungunya arthritis patients, as well as recovered individuals and healthy controls. The study employs flow-cytometry-based assays and statistical methods to analyze the relationship between ADCC activity and antibody levels. Results show that recovered individuals maintain a positive correlation between ADCC response and IgG and IgG3 antibody levels, while chronic arthritis patients exhibit a progressive decline. These findings suggest that NK cell-mediated ADCC is important in chikungunya infection and may support the development of antibody-based therapies. The study's evidence is moderate in strength due to its observational design and potential confounding factors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估自然杀伤(NK)细胞介导的抗体依赖性细胞毒性(ADCC)在基孔肯雅病毒感染中的作用,基于已知ADCC在多种病毒感染清除中的贡献。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了56名急性期、56名持续期和44名慢性基孔肯雅病毒关节炎患者的CHIKV特异性ADCC反应,以及23名恢复期个体和50名健康对照者的反应,以了解NK细胞活性在感染不同阶段的动态变化。
elements_zh.methods: 采用基于流式细胞术的抗体依赖性异源NK细胞激活检测,使用CD107a和IFN-γ作为替代标志物。组间比较采用曼-惠特尼检验,二元数据采用费舍尔精确检验分析,ADCC反应与抗体水平之间的关系采用斯皮尔曼等级相关分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 恢复期个体的ADCC反应与血浆抗CHIKV IgG和IgG3抗体水平呈正相关(IgG: r = 0.4503,IgG3: r = 0.4583,每个p值均<0.01)。在慢性基孔肯雅病毒关节炎患者中观察到ADCC反应逐渐下降,而在恢复期个体中则观察到ADCC反应持续存在,持续时间从感染后3个月到18年不等。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现确立了NK细胞介导的ADCC在基孔肯雅病毒感染中的作用,并突出了IgG3抗体在基于抗体的治疗中的潜力,特别是在长期免疫的背景下。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对基孔肯雅病毒感染免疫机制的见解,并可能为基于抗体的治疗和监测感染个体的策略提供依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究的观察性质以及可能存在的混杂因素,其推广性可能受到一定限制,尽管统计分析支持了这些证据,且其证据强度被认为是中等的。

papers.abstract_zh: 抗体依赖性细胞毒性(ADCC)由自然杀伤(NK)细胞介导,在多种病毒感染的清除过程中已有充分文献记载。除了直接中和病毒外,病毒特异性抗体还通过涉及ADCC的效应功能提供保护。已确认NK细胞是基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)感染中的关键贡献者。本研究通过评估56名急性期、56名持续期和44名慢性基孔肯雅病毒关节炎患者的CHIKV特异性ADCC反应,以及23名恢复期个体和50名健康对照者的反应,来探讨NK细胞介导的ADCC在基孔肯雅病毒感染中的作用。采用基于流式细胞术的抗体依赖性异源NK细胞激活检测,使用CD107a和IFN-γ作为替代标志物。采用曼-惠特尼检验进行组间比较,二元数据采用费舍尔精确检验分析,ADCC反应与CHIKV病毒载量、总抗CHIKV IgG和IgG3抗体水平之间的相关性采用斯皮尔曼等级相关分析。P值<0.05被认为具有统计学意义。在恢复期个体中观察到ADCC反应持续存在,持续时间从感染后3个月到18年不等,而在慢性基孔肯雅病毒关节炎患者中则观察到ADCC反应逐渐下降。在部分急性期患者中,ADCC反应与病毒载量呈负相关。恢复期个体的ADCC反应与血浆抗CHIKV IgG和IgG3抗体水平呈正相关(IgG: r = 0.4503,IgG3: r = 0.4583,每个p值均<0.01)。综上所述,这些发现确立了NK细胞介导的ADCC反应在基孔肯雅病毒感染中的作用,并为未来基于抗体的基孔肯雅病毒治疗奠定了基础,特别是利用具有功能ADCC能力的IgG3抗体。

papers.title: Dengue and Chikungunya Seroprevalence in an Urban Low-Income Cohort in Delhi: A Cross-Sectional and Nested Longitudinal Study
papers.abstract: Objectives: The aim of this study was to ascertain the seroprevalence and determinants of dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) seropositivity in Delhi, India. Methods: This cross-sectional serosurvey with a nested longitudinal immunological sub-study was conducted in an urban resettlement and slum settlement in the North-East district of Delhi in individuals aged ≥2 years. Dengue and Chikungunya virus IgG antibodies were screened using indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and a longitudinal subset of 100 paired IgG-seropositive samples was further characterized via a plaque reduction neutralization test (μPRNT50) to evaluate changes in functional neutralization over time. Results: A total of 752 participants, including 56.65% female participants, were included in the study. Of the participants studied, 81.91% (95% CI: 78.97, 84.60; n = 616) were positive for IgG antibodies against DENV, and 28.32% (95% CI: 25.13, 31.69; n = 213) were positive for CHIKV IgG antibodies. μPRNT50 confirmed stable, near-universal CHIKV neutralization (97% baseline, 98% endline). However, DENV neutralizing antibody showed a significant contraction for DENV-3 (79% baseline, 60% endline) and DENV-4 (69% baseline, 60% endline), while DENV-1 (76%) and DENV-2 (77% to 80%) antibodies remained stable. Individuals living in households with screened windows had significantly lower odds of contracting DENV infection (AOR: 0.36; 95% CI: 0.21, 0.61) and CHIKV infection (AOR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.43, 0.90) compared with those living in households without screened windows. Further, individuals from households with uncovered containers with stagnant water had 50% higher odds of CHIKV infection than those without such containers (AOR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.05, 2.29). Conclusions: This study revealed a high burden of DENV and CHIKV exposure in this high-risk urban population. While neutralization remained stable for CHIKV, DENV-1, and DENV-2, waning DENV-3 and DENV-4 antibodies suggest differential serotype-specific immunity in the participants.

Methods: This cross-sectional serosurvey with a nested longitudinal immunological sub-study was conducted in an urban resettlement and slum settlement in the North-East district of Delhi in individuals aged ≥2 years. Dengue and Chikungunya virus IgG antibodies were screened using indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and a longitudinal subset of 100 paired IgG-seropositive samples was further characterized via a plaque reduction neutralization test (μPRNT50) to evaluate changes in functional neutralization over time. Results: A total of 752 participants, including 56.65% female participants, were included in the study. Of the participants studied, 81.91% (95% CI: 78.97, 84.60; n = 616) were positive for IgG antibodies against DENV, and 28.32% (95% CI: 25.13, 31.69; n = 213) were positive for CHIKV IgG antibodies. μPRNT50 confirmed stable, near-universal CHIKV neutralization (97% baseline, 98% endline). However, DENV neutralizing antibody showed a significant contraction for DENV-3 (79% baseline, 60% endline) and DENV-4 (69% baseline, 60% endline), while DENV-1 (76%) and DENV-2 (77% to 80%) antibodies remained stable. Individuals living in households with screened windows had significantly lower odds of contracting DENV infection (AOR: 0.36; 95% CI: 0.21, 0.61) and CHIKV infection (AOR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.43, 0.90) compared with those living in households without screened windows. Further, individuals from households with uncovered containers with stagnant water had 50% higher odds of CHIKV infection than those without such containers (AOR: 1.55; 95% CI: 1.05, 2.29). Conclusions: This study revealed a high burden of DENV and CHIKV exposure in this high-risk urban population. While neutralization remained stable for CHIKV, DENV-1, and DENV-2, waning DENV-3 and DENV-4 antibodies suggest differential serotype-specific immunity in the participants.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional serosurvey with a nested longitudinal immunological sub-study was conducted in an urban resettlement and slum settlement in the North-East district of Delhi in individuals aged ≥2 years. analysis.methods: Dengue and Chikungunya virus IgG antibodies were screened using indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and a longitudinal subset of 100 paired IgG-seropositive samples was further characterized via a plaque reduction neutralization test (μPRNT50) to evaluate changes in functional neutralization over time.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the seroprevalence and determinants of dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in an urban low-income cohort in Delhi, India. A cross-sectional serosurvey with a nested longitudinal immunological sub-study was conducted among 752 participants aged ≥2 years. DENV and CHIKV IgG antibodies were detected using ELISA, and neutralization was assessed via μPRNT50. Results showed high DENV seroprevalence (81.91%) and moderate CHIKV seroprevalence (28.32%). CHIKV neutralization remained stable, while DENV-3 and DENV-4 neutralizing antibodies decreased. Household factors such as screened windows and uncovered containers with stagnant water were associated with reduced infection risk. The study highlights the need for targeted interventions in high-risk urban areas to mitigate DENV and CHIKV transmission. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the findings are considered moderate in strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在确定血清流行率及其决定因素,以及登革病毒(DENV)和基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)在印度德里的血清阳性率。该研究旨在了解高风险城市人群中DENV和CHIKV暴露的负担。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究为一项横断面血清学调查,并包含嵌套的纵向免疫学子研究,在德里东北区的城市安置区和贫民窟中对年龄≥2岁的个体进行。共有752名参与者,其中女性参与者占56.65%,均被纳入研究。
elements_zh.methods: 采用间接酶联免疫吸附测定(ELISA)筛选了登革热和基孔肯雅病毒 IgG抗体,并通过蚀斑减少中和试验(μPRNT50)对100对配对IgG血清阳性样本的纵向子集进行了进一步表征,以评估功能性中和作用随时间的变化。
elements_zh.main_results: Of the participants studied, 81.91% (95% CI: 78.97, 84.60; n = 616) were positive for IgG antibodies against DENV, and 28.32% (95% CI: 25.13, 31.69; n = 213) were positive for CHIKV IgG antibodies. μPRNT50 confirmed stable, near-universal CHIKV neutralization (97% baseline, 98% endline).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,登革病毒和基孔肯雅病毒在该人群中的高血清流行率表明存在显著暴露。该研究的创新之处在于观察到基孔肯雅病毒中和反应的稳定性以及登革病毒血清型特异性免疫反应的差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为监测的公共卫生策略以及城市低收入人群登革热和基孔肯雅热的预防提供了信息。它们强调了在家庭层面采取干预措施以降低感染风险的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的横断面设计限制了推断因果关系的能力,样本量可能无法充分代表更广泛的人群。由于研究的观察性质以及潜在的混杂因素,证据等级为中等。

papers.title: Epidemiology of Chikungunya Virus Infection in the Philippines
papers.abstract: Background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has circulated in the Philippines for more than six decades. Reviewing the evidence accumulated over this period provides an oppor-tunity to summarize its epidemiology and describe patterns of transmission over time. We systematically reviewed the epidemiology of CHIKV in the Philippines, integrating evidence on transmission, seroprevalence, diagnostics and molecular lineages. Methods: We followed PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed and Embase to March 2026 for original studies reporting incidence, prevalence, seroprevalence, outbreak characteristics, or surveillance findings in human populations in the Philippines. Grey literature from the Department of Health (DOH) Epidemiology Bureau (2018–March 2026) was included separately. Findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity. Results: Sixteen studies and one national surveillance dataset were included. Serological reconstruction and prospective cohorts indicate approximately four major transmission waves over six decades, separated by intervals of about 17 years. Each wave infected an estimated 23% (16–37%) of remaining susceptible, while more than half remained sus-ceptible thereafter. In Cebu, incidence declined from 12.32 to 2.84 infections per 100 person-years as neutralizing-antibody prevalence increased from 28% to 42%; only about one in five infections was symptomatic. National surveillance recorded 12,662 cases from 2018 to early 2026, including 722 laboratory-confirmed; three deaths. The Asian genotype predominated during the 2011–2013 epidemic, while the Indian Ocean lineage viruses were detected in southern Mindanao. Conclusions: Transmission of CHIKV in the Phil-ippines appears to follow a periodic, recurrent pattern, with outbreaks occurring as population susceptibility accumulates following periods of low-level transmission. Pe-riodic arboviral serosurveys and testing of acute febrile illness are needed to better characterize CHIKV epidemiology in the Philippines.

Reviewing the evidence accumulated over this period provides an oppor-tunity to summarize its epidemiology and describe patterns of transmission over time. We systematically reviewed the epidemiology of CHIKV in the Philippines, integrating evidence on transmission, seroprevalence, diagnostics and molecular lineages. Methods: We followed PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed and Embase to March 2026 for original studies reporting incidence, prevalence, seroprevalence, outbreak characteristics, or surveillance findings in human populations in the Philippines. Grey literature from the Department of Health (DOH) Epidemiology Bureau (2018–March 2026) was included separately. Findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity. Results: Sixteen studies and one national surveillance dataset were included. Serological reconstruction and prospective cohorts indicate approximately four major transmission waves over six decades, separated by intervals of about 17 years. Each wave infected an estimated 23% (16–37%) of remaining susceptible, while more than half remained sus-ceptible thereafter. In Cebu, incidence declined from 12.32 to 2.84 infections per 100 person-years as neutralizing-antibody prevalence increased from 28% to 42%; only about one in five infections was symptomatic. National surveillance recorded 12,662 cases from 2018 to early 2026, including 722 laboratory-confirmed; three deaths. The Asian genotype predominated during the 2011–2013 epidemic, while the Indian Ocean lineage viruses were detected in southern Mindanao. Conclusions: Transmission of CHIKV in the Phil-ippines appears to follow a periodic, recurrent pattern, with outbreaks occurring as population susceptibility accumulates following periods of low-level transmission. Pe-riodic arboviral serosurveys and testing of acute febrile illness are needed to better characterize CHIKV epidemiology in the Philippines.

analysis.summary_en: This review summarizes the epidemiology of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in the Philippines, highlighting its long-standing circulation and periodic transmission patterns. The study integrates evidence on transmission, seroprevalence, diagnostics, and molecular lineages, with findings synthesized narratively due to heterogeneity. Sixteen studies and one national surveillance dataset were included, revealing four major transmission waves over six decades, with the Asian genotype dominating the 2011–2013 epidemic and the Indian Ocean lineage detected in southern Mindanao. The review emphasizes the need for periodic serosurveys and acute febrile illness testing to better understand CHIKV dynamics. However, specific mechanisms driving outbreaks and detailed geographic lineage distribution remain unresolved, indicating gaps in current evidence.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 菲律宾的CHIKV似乎呈现出周期性、反复发作的模式,随着低水平传播时期后人群易感性的积累,会出现暴发。2011–2013年流行期间,亚洲基因型占主导地位,而在棉兰老岛南部检测到了印度洋谱系病毒。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 现有证据未报告关于周期性流行的具体驱动机制或环境因素在流行模式中的作用。现有证据也未报告关于不同基孔肯雅病毒谱系的地理分布信息,除了亚洲基因型和印度洋谱系病毒。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要定期进行蚊媒病毒血清学调查和急性发热病例的检测,以更好地描述基孔肯雅病毒在菲律宾的流行病学特征。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)已在菲律宾流行超过六十年。回顾这一时期积累的证据,有助于总结其流行病学特征并描述其流行模式随时间的变化。我们系统地回顾了菲律宾基孔肯雅病毒的流行病学特征,整合了关于流行模式、血清学特征、诊断和分子谱系的证据。方法:我们遵循PRISMA 2020指南,在2026年3月之前检索PubMed和Embase数据库,以获取报告菲律宾人群中基孔肯雅病毒感染率、血清学特征、诊断特征、传播特征或临床表现的原始研究。此外,还单独纳入了菲律宾卫生部(DOH)流行病学局(2018年至2026年3月)的灰色文献。由于存在显著的异质性,研究结果采用叙述性综合方法进行总结。结果:共纳入16项研究和1个全国性流行病学数据集。血清学重建和前瞻性研究显示,在六十年间大约出现了四次主要的流行波,间隔约17年。每次流行波感染了估计剩余易感人群的23%(16%-37%),而超过一半的人群在之后仍保持易感。在宿务,每100人年感染率从12.32降至2.84,同时中和抗体血清学阳性率从28%上升至42%;仅有约五分之一的感染病例出现症状。全国性流行病学记录显示,2018年至2026年初共报告了12,662例病例,包括722例实验室确诊病例和3例死亡。2011年至2013年的流行期间,亚洲基因型占主导地位,而在棉兰老岛南部则检测到印度洋谱系病毒。结论:基孔肯雅病毒在菲律宾的流行似乎遵循周期性、反复出现的模式,当人群易感性积累后,会再次出现流行。因此,需要定期进行蚊媒病毒血清学调查和急性发热病例的检测,以更好地描述基孔肯雅病毒在菲律宾的流行病学特征。

papers.title: Autochthonous chikungunya virus (CHIKV) outbreak in the province of Modena, Emilia-Romagna region, Italy, August to October 2025: epidemiology, clinical features and virological findings
papers.abstract: Between 10 August and 31 October 2025, 343 cases (306 confirmed and 37 probable) of symptomatic autochthonous chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection were notified in eight municipalities in the province of Modena, Emilia-Romagna region, northern Italy. The infection was diagnosed by detection of CHIKV RNA in blood and urine samples, and by detection of IgM antibodies against CHIKV. Most common symptoms were arthralgia (n = 326) and fever (n = 317). No fatalities were reported. Chikungunya virus RNA was detected in 39 (14.8%) of 263 pools of Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, thereby confirming local vector-borne transmission. Sequences from 11 case samples and two mosquito pools were whole genome sequenced. The viral strain belonged to the East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineage 2 and was closely related to the strains circulating in Reunion Island in 2024–25. The public health response included rapid vector control measures, reinforced epidemiological surveillance and multidisciplinary coordination between public health authorities and clinicians, laboratories and entomologists. This was one of the largest autochthonous CHIKV outbreaks ever recorded in a temperate European region. It highlights the critical importance of integrated, multidisciplinary preparedness and response for arboviral threats in non-endemic areas.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突显了在非流行地区应对虫媒病毒威胁时,整合多学科准备和响应措施的重要性。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受到观察性设计和潜在报告不足的限制,但由于采用了全面的方法并通过对蚊虫池的检测确认了本地传播,其证据是强有力的。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查意大利摩德纳省本地传播的基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)疫情的流行病学特征、临床表现和病毒学发现,以更好地了解该病毒在温带地区的出现和传播情况。
analysis_zh.methods: 感染通过在血液和尿液样本中检测到CHIKV RNA以及检测到针对CHIKV的IgM抗体进行诊断。公共卫生应对措施包括快速的媒介控制措施、加强的流行病学监测以及公共卫生机构与临床医生、实验室和昆虫学家之间的多学科协作。
analysis_zh.main_results: 最常见的症状是关节痛(n = 326)和发热(n = 317)。未报告死亡病例。在263个Aedes albopictus蚊虫池中,检测到39个(14.8%)含有CHIKV RNA,从而确认了本地传播的基孔肯雅病毒。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突显了在非流行地区应对虫媒病毒威胁时,整合多学科准备和响应措施的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究提供了关于基孔肯雅病毒在欧洲温带地区流行病学和临床特征的见解,这些信息可用于监测、防控和制定类似疫情的公共卫生策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受到观察性设计和潜在报告不足的限制,但由于采用了全面的方法并通过对蚊虫池的检测确认了本地传播,其证据是强有力的。

papers.title: Antigenic and genetic analysis of 2025 Chikungunya virus outbreak in China
papers.abstract: The 2025 Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) epidemic in China, primarily driven by the East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineage, has resulted in over 25,600 infections and one fatality, highlighting a significant public health threat. To elucidate the virological and immunological drivers of this outbreak, a comprehensive in silico investigation was conducted, integrating epidemiological, phylogenetic, and immunoinformatic data across 4,662 sequences. Phylogenetic analysis reveals that the outbreak likely originated from limited recent introductions, with the ECSA lineage comprising approximately 70% of the imported isolates. Temporal tracking of B-cell epitopes indicates an increase in mutation frequencies within the E1 and E2 glycoproteins since 2016. However, mapping against 38 known neutralizing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) demonstrates that only six mutations in the 2025 E2 protein affect mAb binding sites, with just one mutation (L210Q) impacting a major epitope cluster. This indicates that the circulating variants have not yet achieved substantial B-cell immune escape. Furthermore, T-cell epitope profiling uncovers a critical population-level genetic vulnerability. While individuals with highly frequent alleles like HLA-A*02:01 are predicted to present abundant epitopes for a robust T-cell response, prevalent HLA-C alleles in the Chinese population (HLA-C*07:02 and HLA-C*01:02) present a critically low number of CHIKV epitopes. This reduced capacity for T-cell-mediated viral clearance in a substantial demographic underscores the necessity for prophylactic measures tailored to specific genetic vulnerabilities. Consequently, future vaccine development must focus on eliciting broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies while incorporating promiscuous T-cell epitopes to protect these vulnerable populations.

papers.title_zh: 2025 基孔肯雅病毒 暴发在中国的抗原和遗传分析
papers.source_body_en: The 2025 Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) epidemic in China, primarily driven by the East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineage, has resulted in over 25,600 infections and one fatality, highlighting a significant public health threat. To elucidate the virological and immunological drivers of this outbreak, a comprehensive in silico investigation was conducted, integrating epidemiological, phylogenetic, and immunoinformatic data across 4,662 sequences. Phylogenetic analysis reveals that the outbreak likely originated from limited recent introductions, with the ECSA lineage comprising approximately 70% of the imported isolates. Temporal tracking of B-cell epitopes indicates an increase in mutation frequencies within the E1 and E2 glycoproteins since 2016. However, mapping against 38 known neutralizing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) demonstrates that only six mutations in the 2025 E2 protein affect mAb binding sites, with just one mutation (L210Q) impacting a major epitope cluster. This indicates that the circulating variants have not yet achieved substantial B-cell immune escape. Furthermore, T-cell epitope profiling uncovers a critical population-level genetic vulnerability. While individuals with highly frequent alleles like HLA-A*02:01 are predicted to present abundant epitopes for a robust T-cell response, prevalent HLA-C alleles in the Chinese population (HLA-C*07:02 and HLA-C*01:02) present a critically low number of CHIKV epitopes. This reduced capacity for T-cell-mediated viral clearance in a substantial demographic underscores the necessity for prophylactic measures tailored to specific genetic vulnerabilities. Consequently, future vaccine development must focus on eliciting broad-spectrum neutralizing antibodies while incorporating promiscuous T-cell epitopes to protect these vulnerable populations.
papers.abstract_zh: 2025年中国基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)暴发主要由东/中/非(ECSA)谱系驱动,已导致超过25,600例感染和1例死亡,凸显了重大的公共卫生威胁。为阐明此次暴发的病毒学和免疫学驱动因素,本研究开展了一项全面的计算机模拟分析,整合了4,662条序列的流行病学、系统发育及免疫信息学数据。系统发育分析表明,此次暴发可能源于近期有限的输入事件,其中ECSA谱系约占输入分离株的70%。B细胞表位的时序追踪显示,自2016年以来E1和E2糖蛋白中突变的频率有所增加。然而,与38种已知中和性单克隆抗体(mAbs)的比对表明,2025年E2蛋白中仅有六个突变影响mAb结合位点,其中仅有一个突变(L210Q)影响主要表位簇。这表明当前循环变异株尚未实现显著的B细胞免疫逃逸。此外,T细胞表位分析揭示了一个关键的群体水平遗传易感性。虽然携带高频等位基因(如HLA-A*02:01)的个体预计能呈递丰富的表位以产生强效T细胞免疫应答,但中国人群中常见的HLA-C等位基因(HLA-C*07:02和HLA-C*01:02)呈递的CHIKV表位数量极低。这一相当大的人群中T细胞介导的病毒清除能力降低,凸显了针对特定遗传易感性制定预防措施的必要性。因此,未来疫苗的开发必须侧重于诱导广谱中和抗体,同时纳入多态性T细胞表位,以保护这些易感人群。

papers.title: Development of Covalent Inhibitors of Chikungunya Virus nsP2 Cysteine Protease Enabled by Direct-to-Biology Synthesis and Screening.
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus, has emerged as a global health threat due to its rapid transmission and the lack of effective antiviral therapies. The cysteine protease activity of the virus-encoded nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) is critical for CHIKV replication, as it processes viral polyproteins and counteracts host antiviral defenses, establishing it as a highly attractive target for therapeutic intervention. In this study, we present a rapid drug development platform that integrates covalent docking with direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis and screening to identify nsP2 inhibitors. Candidates prioritized by in silico docking were synthesized and directly tested in FRET enzymatic assays without purification. This approach led to the identification of several nsP2 inhibitors with diverse chemical scaffolds, potent enzymatic inhibition, and antiviral activity. Together, these findings establish a streamlined strategy for covalent inhibitor development and provide promising leads for CHIKV antiviral development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a globally emerging arbovirus lacking effective antiviral therapies, and the essential role of its nsP2 cysteine protease in replication makes it an attractive therapeutic target.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a rapid drug development platform that combines covalent docking with direct‐to‐biology synthesis and screening to discover nsP2 inhibitors.
analysis.methods: Prioritized compounds from in silico docking were synthesized and evaluated directly in fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) enzymatic assays without purification.
analysis.main_results: The approach yielded several nsP2 inhibitors with diverse scaffolds that showed potent enzymatic inhibition and antiviral activity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that this streamlined covalent inhibitor development strategy provides promising leads for CHIKV antiviral therapy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a viable pathway for accelerating antiviral discovery against CHIKV, which could enhance future therapeutic options.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report any study limitations or an assessment of evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the urgent need for chikungunya virus (CHIKV) therapeutics by targeting the essential nsP2 cysteine protease. Researchers implemented a rapid drug development platform that merges covalent docking with direct‐to‐biology synthesis, allowing prioritized compounds to be synthesized and screened in FRET enzymatic assays without purification. The workflow identified multiple diverse scaffolds that potently inhibit nsP2 activity and demonstrate antiviral effects in vitro. The authors interpret these results as establishing a streamlined strategy for covalent inhibitor development, offering promising leads for CHIKV antiviral therapy. While the approach could accelerate future antiviral discovery and expand therapeutic options for CHIKV, the provided evidence does not detail any study limitations or evaluate the overall strength of the evidence.

papers.title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV)的nsP2半胱氨酸蛋白酶共价抑制剂的开发,通过直接到生物学合成和筛选实现.
papers.source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus, has emerged as a global health threat due to its rapid transmission and the lack of effective antiviral therapies. The cysteine protease activity of the virus-encoded nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) is critical for CHIKV replication, as it processes viral polyproteins and counteracts host antiviral defenses, establishing it as a highly attractive target for therapeutic intervention. In this study, we present a rapid drug development platform that integrates covalent docking with direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis and screening to identify nsP2 inhibitors. Candidates prioritized by in silico docking were synthesized and directly tested in FRET enzymatic assays without purification. This approach led to the identification of several nsP2 inhibitors with diverse chemical scaffolds, potent enzymatic inhibition, and antiviral activity. Together, these findings establish a streamlined strategy for covalent inhibitor development and provide promising leads for CHIKV antiviral development.
papers.abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),一种通过昆虫传播的α病毒,已成为全球健康威胁之一,主要原因是其快速的 传播 以及缺乏有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法。病毒编码的非结构蛋白2(nsP2)的半胱氨酸蛋白酶活性对 CHIKV 的复制至关重要,因为它加工病毒多聚蛋白并抵消 宿主 抗病毒药物 的防御机制,使其成为治疗干预的高度吸引目标。在本研究中,我们提出了一套快速的药物开发平台,该平台整合了共价锁定与直接到生物学(D2B)合成和筛选,以识别 nsP2 抑制剂。通过体外计算锁定优先级的候选分子被合成并在不进行纯化的 FRET 酶学试验中直接测试。这一方法导致了多个具有多样化学骨架、强效酶抑制作用且具有 抗病毒药物 活性的 nsP2 抑制剂的鉴定。总的来说,这些发现建立了一种用于共价抑制剂开发的简化策略,并为 CHIKV 抗病毒药物 开发提供了有希望的线索。

papers.title: DIAGNÓSTICO E ASPECTOS FISIOPATOLÓGICOS DA ARTRITE PÓS CHIKUNGUNYA
papers.abstract: Chikungunya é uma arbovirose causada pelo vírus CHIKV que pode desencadear manifestações crônicas como a artrite. Este estudo trata-se de uma revisão integrativa sobre o diagnóstico e aspectos fisiopatológicos da artrite pós-Chikungunya, a fim de aprofundar o entendimento do tema e orientar estudos futuros focados na melhora da qualidade de vida do paciente. A pesquisa foi conduzida nas bases PubMed, SciELO e BVS, utilizando os descritores “Vírus Chikungunya”, “Febre de Chikungunya”, “Artrite” e “Diagnóstico diferencial”, segundo os Descritores em Ciências da Saúde (DeCS). Foram incluídos 16 artigos originais publicados entre 2017 e 2026, que atendiam aos critérios de elegibilidade previamente estabelecidos. Foram excluídos estudos de revisão ou fora do escopo. Os resultados evidenciaram que a artrite pós-Chikungunya é caracterizada por sintomas articulares persistentes e pode durar meses ou anos após a fase aguda da infecção. O diagnóstico clínico é fundamental e, na fase aguda, pode ser confirmado por RT-PCR ou sorologia (IgM/IgG), enquanto na fase crônica a avaliação baseia-se na persistência dos sintomas e na exclusão de outras doenças reumatológicas. Os estudos revisados apontam que a fisiopatologia da doença envolve uma resposta inflamatória exacerbada, com elevação de citocinas como IL-6, IL-1β, IL-17 e TNF-α, além da persistência do RNA viral nos tecidos sinoviais e ativação de vias osteoclastogênicas, que levam à inflamação articular crônica e degradação óssea. Conclui-se que a artrite pós-Chikungunya é uma condição inflamatória crônica com manifestações articulares persistentes, cuja complexidade demanda maior atenção clínica e aprofundamento científico para o aprimoramento das estratégias diagnósticas e terapêuticas.

Este estudo trata-se de uma revisão integrativa sobre o diagnóstico e aspectos fisiopatológicos da artrite pós-Chikungunya, a fim de aprofundar o entendimento do tema e orientar estudos futuros focados na melhora da qualidade de vida do paciente. A pesquisa foi conduzida nas bases PubMed, SciELO e BVS, utilizando os descritores “Vírus Chikungunya”, “Febre de Chikungunya”, “Artrite” e “Diagnóstico diferencial”, segundo os Descritores em Ciências da Saúde (DeCS). Foram incluídos 16 artigos originais publicados entre 2017 e 2026, que atendiam aos critérios de elegibilidade previamente estabelecidos. Foram excluídos estudos de revisão ou fora do escopo. Os resultados evidenciaram que a artrite pós-Chikungunya é caracterizada por sintomas articulares persistentes e pode durar meses ou anos após a fase aguda da infecção. O diagnóstico clínico é fundamental e, na fase aguda, pode ser confirmado por RT-PCR ou sorologia (IgM/IgG), enquanto na fase crônica a avaliação baseia-se na persistência dos sintomas e na exclusão de outras doenças reumatológicas. Os estudos revisados apontam que a fisiopatologia da doença envolve uma resposta inflamatória exacerbada, com elevação de citocinas como IL-6, IL-1β, IL-17 e TNF-α, além da persistência do RNA viral nos tecidos sinoviais e ativação de vias osteoclastogênicas, que levam à inflamação articular crônica e degradação óssea. Conclui-se que a artrite pós-Chikungunya é uma condição inflamatória crônica com manifestações articulares persistentes, cuja complexidade demanda maior atenção clínica e aprofundamento científico para o aprimoramento das estratégias diagnósticas e terapêuticas.

analysis.summary_en: This study is a comprehensive review of the diagnostic and pathophysiological aspects of post-Chikungunya arthritis, aiming to deepen understanding and guide future research focused on improving patient quality of life. The research was conducted using PubMed, SciELO, and BVS databases with specific descriptors related to Chikungunya virus and arthritis. Sixteen original articles published between 2017 and 2026 were included, while reviews and out-of-scope studies were excluded. The study highlights that post-Chikungunya arthritis is characterized by persistent joint symptoms that can last months or years after the acute phase of infection. It also identifies a pathophysiological mechanism involving an exacerbated inflammatory response, elevated cytokines such as IL-6, IL-1β, IL-17, and TNF-α, as well as the persistence of viral RNA in synovial tissues and activation of osteoclastogenic pathways, leading to chronic joint inflammation and bone degradation. The findings emphasize the need for increased clinical attention and further scientific research to enhance diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. However, the evidence is based on reviewed studies rather than primary data, which may limit the generalizability of the results. The study provides moderate confidence in its conclusions due to the reliance on secondary sources and the absence of direct experimental data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基孔肯雅热是一种由基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)引起的虫媒病毒病,可引发关节炎等慢性表现。本研究为一篇关于基孔肯雅热后关节炎诊断与病理生理学特征的整合性综述,旨在深化对该主题的理解,并为未来聚焦于改善患者生活质量的研究提供指导。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究在PubMed、SciELO和BVS数据库中进行,使用了‘基孔肯雅病毒’、‘基孔肯雅热’、‘关节痛’和‘鉴别诊断’等术语,依据卫生科学关键词(DeCS)。共纳入16篇原创文章,发表时间在2017年至2026年之间,符合之前确定的纳入标准。排除了综述研究或超出范围的研究。

elements_zh.main_results: 所综述的研究指出,该病的发病机制涉及过度炎症反应,表现为IL-6、IL-1β、IL-17和TNF-α等细胞因子的升高,以及病毒RNA在滑膜组织中的持续存在和破骨细胞生成通路的激活,从而导致慢性关节炎症和骨降解。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果表明,基孔肯雅热后关节炎以持续性关节症状为特征,可在感染急性期后持续数月或数年。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 基孔肯雅热后关节炎是一种具有持续性关节表现的慢性炎症性疾病,其复杂性需要更多的临床关注和科学深入,以改进诊断和治疗策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基于所综述的研究而非原始数据,限制了研究发现的推广性。

papers.abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅热是由基孔肯雅病毒引起的一种虫媒病毒性疾病,可能引发慢性表现如关节炎。本研究是一项关于基孔肯雅热后关节炎诊断及发病机制的综合文献回顾,旨在深入理解该主题并指导未来以改善患者生活质量为中心的研究。研究在PubMed、SciELO和BVS数据库中进行,使用了“基孔肯雅病毒”、“基孔肯雅热”、“关节炎”和“鉴别诊断”等关键词,依据巴西卫生科学关键词(DeCS)进行检索。共纳入了16篇符合既定纳入标准的原创文章,发表时间范围为2017年至2026年,排除了综述文章或超出研究范围的文献。研究结果表明,基孔肯雅热后关节炎以持续性关节症状为特征,可能在急性感染期后持续数月甚至数年。临床诊断至关重要,在急性期可通过RT-PCR或血清学检测(IgM/IgG)进行确认,而在慢性期则基于症状的持续存在及排除其他风湿性疾病。综述研究指出,该病的发病机制涉及过度的炎症反应,表现为IL-6、IL-1β、IL-17和TNF-α等细胞因子水平升高,同时病毒RNA在滑膜组织中持续存在,并激活破骨途径,导致慢性关节炎和骨质破坏。结论认为,基孔肯雅热后关节炎是一种具有持续性关节表现的慢性炎症性疾病,其复杂性需要更多的临床关注和科学研究,以优化诊断和治疗策略。

papers.full_text: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. albopictus. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. albopictus. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study provides an overview of the epidemiology, biology, and pathogenesis of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), highlighting its global spread and the need for improved understanding to inform public health strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a comprehensive review of CHIKV, focusing on its transmission, replication, and clinical manifestations. It includes data from outbreaks in the Americas and reports on the virus's genetic structure and associated diseases.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a detailed analysis of CHIKV's molecular structure, replication mechanisms, and epidemiological patterns. The study also references existing literature on vaccine development and therapeutic approaches.
analysis.main_results: Since its introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence of CHIKV remains high, with over 180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the continued high incidence as a reflection of the virus's adaptability and the challenges in controlling its spread. The novelty lies in the integration of molecular, epidemiological, and clinical data to provide a holistic understanding of CHIKV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of preventive strategies, including vector control and vaccine research, and highlight the need for improved surveillance and management of CHIKV outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on existing literature and does not include new experimental data, which may limit the strength of its conclusions. However, the evidence is robust and derived from multiple sources, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides a comprehensive overview of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), focusing on its epidemiology, biology, and pathogenesis. It highlights the virus's global spread, particularly in the Americas since 2013, with over 180,000 confirmed cases in 2025. The review details CHIKV's structure, replication mechanisms, and clinical manifestations, emphasizing the need for improved understanding to guide public health strategies. The authors interpret the continued high incidence as a result of the virus's adaptability and challenges in control. They note the importance of vector control and vaccine development, while acknowledging the lack of licensed antivirals. The study's findings are based on existing literature, which may limit the strength of its conclusions, but the evidence is robust and supports a moderate confidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究概述了基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)的传播、生物学和流行病学,突出了其全球传播和对公共卫生策略改进理解的必要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是对 CHIKV 的全面综述,重点探讨其传播、复制和临床表现。它包括美洲地区的传播数据以及关于病毒基因组结构和相关疾病的报告。
elements_zh.methods: 研究方法包括对 CHIKV 分子结构、复制机制和流行病学模式的详细分析。该研究还参考了现有文献中关于病毒样颗粒疫苗开发和治疗方案的研究。
elements_zh.main_results: 自 2013 年引入美洲以来,CHIKV 的全球传播率一直很高,2025 年报告了超过 180,000 例确诊病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将持续的高传播率解释为病毒适应性的体现以及控制其传播的挑战。该研究的创新之处在于整合了分子、流行病学和临床数据,以提供对 CHIKV 的全面理解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为预防策略的制定提供了信息,包括媒介控制和疫苗研究,并强调了改善 CHIKV 监测和管理的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于现有文献,未包含新的实验数据,这可能限制其结论的强度。然而,证据是稳健的,并来源于多个来源,支持中等程度的置信度评估。

analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of preventive strategies, including vector control and vaccine research, and highlight the need for improved surveillance and management of CHIKV outbreaks.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on existing literature and does not include new experimental data, which may limit the strength of its conclusions. However, the evidence is robust and derived from multiple sources, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究概述了基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)的传播、生物学和流行病学,突出了其全球传播和对公共卫生策略改进理解的必要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是对 CHIKV 的全面综述,重点探讨其传播、复制和临床表现。它包括美洲地区的传播数据以及关于病毒基因组结构和相关疾病的报告。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究方法包括对 CHIKV 分子结构、复制机制和流行病学模式的详细分析。该研究还参考了现有文献中关于病毒样颗粒疫苗开发和治疗方案的研究。
analysis_zh.main_results: 自 2013 年引入美洲以来,CHIKV 的全球传播率一直很高,2025 年报告了超过 180,000 例确诊病例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将持续的高传播率解释为病毒适应性的体现以及控制其传播的挑战。该研究的创新之处在于整合了分子、流行病学和临床数据,以提供对 CHIKV 的全面理解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为预防策略的制定提供了信息,包括媒介控制和疫苗研究,并强调了改善 CHIKV 监测和管理的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于现有文献,未包含新的实验数据,这可能限制其结论的强度。然而,证据是稳健的,并来源于多个来源,支持中等程度的置信度评估。

papers.title: On the Geographic Spread of Chikungunya Between Brazil and Florida: A Multipatch Model with Time Delay
papers.abstract: Chikungunya (CHIK) is a viral disease transmitted to humans through the bites of Aedes mosquitoes infected with the chikungunya virus (CHIKV). CHIKV has been imported annually to Florida in the last decade due to Miami’s crucial location as a hub for international travel, particularly from Central and South America, including Brazil, where CHIK is endemic. This work addresses the geographic spread of CHIK, incorporating factors such as human movement, temperature dependency, as well as vertical transmission, and incubation periods, for different patches. Central to the model is the integration of a multipatch framework and the inclusion of human movement between endemic Brazilian states and Florida in the numerical analysis. papers.abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅热(CHIK)是一种通过感染了基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)的伊蚊叮咬传播给人类的病毒性疾病。在过去十年中,由于迈阿密作为国际旅行枢纽的关键位置,CHIKV每年都会被引入佛罗里达州,特别是来自包括巴西在内的中美洲和南美洲地区,这些地区是CHIK的流行区。本研究探讨了CHIK在地理上的传播,考虑了诸如人类流动、温度依赖性以及垂直传播的CHIKV和潜伏期等因素在不同区域的影响。模型的核心在于整合多斑块框架,并在数值分析中纳入从流行巴西州到佛罗里达州的人类流动。我们建立了在多斑块环境中蚊虫繁殖数 [Formula: see text] 与疾病繁殖数 [Formula: see text] 之间的关键关联,不仅从理论角度,也通过数值模拟来探讨疾病动态。更具体地说,在确立多斑块模型问题的适定性之后,我们提出了确保疾病持续传播的条件。接下来,利用真实的人口和温度数据,我们能够确定巴西和迈阿密-达德县中所有温度依赖性的参数,并应用一个两斑块模型来校准巴西和迈阿密-达德县的CHIK数据。最后,通过敏感性分析,我们讨论了在不同情景下的疾病动态,并进行了未来预测,为潜在有效的控制策略提供了见解,同时探讨了这些策略实施的时间节点。

papers.title: How Alphaviruses Modulate Host Gene Expression: A Systematic-Narrative Synthesis of Host-Virus Response, Key Genes, and Potential Therapeutic Targets
papers.abstract: Alphaviruses are positive-sense single-stranded RNA viruses belonging to the family Togaviridae; they are also part of the non-taxonomic group of arboviruses and constitute a group of arboviruses of major which are of great clinical and epidemiological relevance worldwide. These viruses can be broadly classified into encephalitic and arthritogenic alphaviruses. Important examples include Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Mayaro virus (MAYV), Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), Ross River virus (RRV), Sindbis virus (SINV), and Semliki Forest virus (SFV), among others. Despite their substantial impact on global public health, characterized by the risk of new outbreaks, high transmission rates, and frequently debilitating or potentially fatal clinical manifestations, effective and specific therapeutic options, including antivirals and vaccines, remain limited for most alphavirus infections. This represents an important public health vulnerability, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. To address this concerning scenario, a comprehensive understanding of the complex interactions between alphaviruses and their hosts is essential for identifying determinants of viral pathogenicity and, consequently, factors associated with disease severity. In this context, transcriptomic and gene expression profiling approaches have become valuable tools for investigating host responses to viral infection. These approaches provide high-resolution information on changes in host gene expression during Alphavirus infection, contributing to the elucidation of molecular mechanisms underlying disease pathogenesis. They can also provide important insights into the identification of biomarkers and molecular signatures, the upregulation or downregulation of specific genes, and the modulation of inflammatory, oxidative, immune, and other biological pathways. Accordingly, this review provides a comprehensive systematic-narrative synthesis of studies investigating alphavirus–host interactions through gene expression profiling. Studies assessing host gene expression in response to alphavirus infection using approaches such as RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), microarrays, RT-qPCR, and other relevant gene expression technologies will be considered across different host species, tissues, experimental models, and infection conditions. Particular emphasis will be placed on studies investigating how alphaviruses modulate key pathogenic pathways, immune responses, inflammation, tissue-specific damage, and other biological processes associated with infection. By integrating evidence from host gene expression profiles, this review aims to highlight the major transcriptional alterations and biological pathways associated with alphavirus pathogenesis. Such integration may provide insights into virus–host interactions and support the identification of candidate molecular targets for therapeutic development, early diagnostic tools, and effective preventive strategies. Therefore, the general objective of this study is to integrate the available evidence on the modulation of host gene expression during alphavirus infection, seeking to elucidate virus–host interactions, molecular mechanisms associated with pathogenesis, and potential key factors involved in these processes. The specific objectives are to: Describe the state of the art regarding alphavirus infections, providing a clinical and epidemiological context for these viruses; Characterize host transcriptional responses to alphavirus infection, identifying similarities and differences in the molecular mechanisms activated or suppressed across different alphaviruses and host systems; Describe molecular mechanisms associated with alphavirus pathogenesis and other biological processes through the integration of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and enriched biological pathways; Map relevant genes and biological pathways associated with different stages and processes of alphavirus infection, across different experimental systems, including in vitro, in vivo, and publicly available transcriptomic datasets; Identify key genes and molecular factors involved in alphavirus–host interactions and explore their potential as therapeutic targets; Identify knowledge gaps, recurrent patterns, and sources of heterogeneity in the existing literature on alphavirus-associated host gene expression. Through this integrative approach, the review is expected to generate sufficient evidence to support hypotheses and future investigations into therapeutic interventions, including the manipulation, editing, or silencing of specific host genes whose modulation or inhibition may impair viral replication while preserving host-cell or host-organism viability. Keywords: alphaviruses; host-virus response; transcriptomics; molecular mechanisms; differential gene expression; viral pathogenesis

analysis.research_question_and_background: Alphaviruses are significant pathogens with major clinical and epidemiological relevance, yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. This study aims to address the need for understanding host-virus interactions to identify potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This systematic-narrative synthesis reviews studies on alphavirus–host interactions, focusing on gene expression profiling across different host species, tissues, experimental models, and infection conditions. It includes studies on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and related entities such as Mayaro virus, Ross River virus, and Sindbis virus.
analysis.methods: The review considers studies using transcriptomic and gene expression profiling approaches, including RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), microarrays, RT-qPCR, and other relevant technologies. These methods are applied across various host systems and experimental models to characterize host responses to alphavirus infection.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights the substantial impact of alphaviruses on global public health, including the risk of new outbreaks, high transmission rates, and debilitating or potentially fatal clinical manifestations. It identifies key pathogenic pathways and molecular mechanisms associated with alphavirus infections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that understanding host gene expression changes during alphavirus infection can reveal critical molecular mechanisms underlying pathogenesis. This review provides a novel integrative perspective on virus–host interactions and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of therapeutic interventions, including strategies to modulate or inhibit specific host genes that may impair viral replication while preserving host viability. They also support the identification of diagnostic tools and preventive strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence and relies on the integration of existing literature. The evidence strength is moderate, as it is based on a review of transcriptomic data rather than original experimental findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the need for understanding host-virus interactions to identify therapeutic targets for alphavirus infections, particularly Chikungunya virus. It reviews transcriptomic and gene expression profiling studies across various host systems and experimental models, highlighting key molecular mechanisms and pathogenic pathways. The findings suggest that modulating host gene expression could offer new strategies for therapeutic development, early diagnosis, and prevention. However, the study is limited to abstract-level evidence and relies on existing literature, which may introduce some uncertainty. The review emphasizes the importance of integrating gene expression data to uncover insights into viral pathogenesis and support future research directions.
