elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 甲型病毒是具有重要临床和流行病学意义的病原体,但有效的治疗方案仍十分有限。本研究旨在通过了解宿主病毒与宿主的相互作用,以识别潜在的治疗靶点。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项系统性叙述性综合分析回顾了关于阿尔法病毒与宿主相互作用的研究,重点审查了不同宿主物种、组织、实验模型和感染条件下的基因表达谱。它包括关于基孔肯雅病毒(基孔肯雅病毒)及其相关实体如马亚罗病毒、罗斯河病毒和辛德毕斯病毒的研究。
elements_zh.methods: 该综述考虑了使用转录组学和基因表达谱分析方法的研究,包括RNA测序(RNA-seq)、单细胞RNA测序(scRNA-seq)、微阵列、逆转录定量PCR(RT-qPCR)以及其他相关技术。这些方法被应用于各种宿主系统和实验模型,以表征宿主对甲型病毒的感染反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 该综述强调了甲型病毒对全球公共卫生的显著影响,包括新暴发的风险、高传播率以及导致严重残疾或潜在致命的临床表现。它确定了与甲型病毒感染相关的关键致病途径和分子机制。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,了解宿主基因在甲病毒感染期间的表达变化可以揭示发病机制的关键分子机制。本综述提供了关于病毒–宿主相互作用及潜在治疗靶点的新颖整合视角。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为治疗干预措施的开发提供信息,包括调节或抑制特定宿主基因的策略,这些基因可能损害病毒复制,同时保持宿主的存活能力。它们还支持诊断工具和预防策略的识别。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于摘要层面的证据,并依赖于现有文献的整合。证据强度中等,因为其基于转录组数据的综述,而非原始实验发现。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Alphaviruses are significant pathogens with major clinical and epidemiological relevance, yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. This study aims to address the need for understanding host-virus interactions to identify potential therapeutic targets.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This systematic-narrative synthesis reviews studies on alphavirus–host interactions, focusing on gene expression profiling across different host species, tissues, experimental models, and infection conditions. It includes studies on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and related entities such as Mayaro virus, Ross River virus, and Sindbis virus.
analysis_en.methods: The review considers studies using transcriptomic and gene expression profiling approaches, including RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), microarrays, RT-qPCR, and other relevant technologies. These methods are applied across various host systems and experimental models to characterize host responses to alphavirus infection.
analysis_en.main_results: The review highlights the substantial impact of alphaviruses on global public health, including the risk of new outbreaks, high transmission rates, and debilitating or potentially fatal clinical manifestations. It identifies key pathogenic pathways and molecular mechanisms associated with alphavirus infections.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that understanding host gene expression changes during alphavirus infection can reveal critical molecular mechanisms underlying pathogenesis. This review provides a novel integrative perspective on virus–host interactions and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of therapeutic interventions, including strategies to modulate or inhibit specific host genes that may impair viral replication while preserving host viability. They also support the identification of diagnostic tools and preventive strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence and relies on the integration of existing literature. The evidence strength is moderate, as it is based on a review of transcriptomic data rather than original experimental findings.

papers.title_zh: 甲型病毒如何调节宿主基因表达:对宿主-病毒反应、关键基因和潜在治疗靶点的系统叙述性综合分析
papers.source_body_en: Alphaviruses are positive-sense single-stranded RNA viruses belonging to the family Togaviridae; they are also part of the non-taxonomic group of arboviruses and constitute a group of arboviruses of major which are of great clinical and epidemiological relevance worldwide. These viruses can be broadly classified into encephalitic and arthritogenic alphaviruses. Important examples include Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Mayaro virus (MAYV), Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), Ross River virus (RRV), Sindbis virus (SINV), and Semliki Forest virus (SFV), among others. Despite their substantial impact on global public health, characterized by the risk of new outbreaks, high transmission rates, and frequently debilitating or potentially fatal clinical manifestations, effective and specific therapeutic options, including antivirals and vaccines, remain limited for most alphavirus infections. This represents an important public health vulnerability, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. To address this concerning scenario, a comprehensive understanding of the complex interactions between alphaviruses and their hosts is essential for identifying determinants of viral pathogenicity and, consequently, factors associated with disease severity. In this context, transcriptomic and gene expression profiling approaches have become valuable tools for investigating host responses to viral infection. These approaches provide high-resolution information on changes in host gene expression during Alphavirus infection, contributing to the elucidation of molecular mechanisms underlying disease pathogenesis. They can also provide important insights into the identification of biomarkers and molecular signatures, the upregulation or downregulation of specific genes, and the modulation of inflammatory, oxidative, immune, and other biological pathways. Accordingly, this review provides a comprehensive systematic-narrative synthesis of studies investigating alphavirus–host interactions through gene expression profiling. Studies assessing host gene expression in response to alphavirus infection using approaches such as RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), microarrays, RT-qPCR, and other relevant gene expression technologies will be considered across different host species, tissues, experimental models, and infection conditions. Particular emphasis will be placed on studies investigating how alphaviruses modulate key pathogenic pathways, immune responses, inflammation, tissue-specific damage, and other biological processes associated with infection. By integrating evidence from host gene expression profiles, this review aims to highlight the major transcriptional alterations and biological pathways associated with alphavirus pathogenesis. Such integration may provide insights into virus–host interactions and support the identification of candidate molecular targets for therapeutic development, early diagnostic tools, and effective preventive strategies. Therefore, the general objective of this study is to integrate the available evidence on the modulation of host gene expression during alphavirus infection, seeking to elucidate virus–host interactions, molecular mechanisms associated with pathogenesis, and potential key factors involved in these processes. The specific objectives are to: Describe the state of the art regarding alphavirus infections, providing a clinical and epidemiological context for these viruses; Characterize host transcriptional responses to alphavirus infection, identifying similarities and differences in the molecular mechanisms activated or suppressed across different alphaviruses and host systems; Describe molecular mechanisms associated with alphavirus pathogenesis and other biological processes through the integration of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and enriched biological pathways; Map relevant genes and biological pathways associated with different stages and processes of alphavirus infection, across different experimental systems, including in vitro, in vivo, and publicly available transcriptomic datasets; Identify key genes and molecular factors involved in alphavirus–host interactions and explore their potential as therapeutic targets; Identify knowledge gaps, recurrent patterns, and sources of heterogeneity in the existing literature on alphavirus-associated host gene expression. Through this integrative approach, the review is expected to generate sufficient evidence to support hypotheses and future investigations into therapeutic interventions, including the manipulation, editing, or silencing of specific host genes whose modulation or inhibition may impair viral replication while preserving host-cell or host-organism viability. Keywords: alphaviruses; host-virus response; transcriptomics; molecular mechanisms; differential gene expression; viral pathogenesis
papers.abstract_zh: 甲型病毒是属于甲型病毒科的正链单股RNA病毒;它们也属于非分类学的虫媒病毒群,构成了具有全球临床和流行病学重要性的主要虫媒病毒群。这些病毒可以大致分为引起脑炎和关节痛的甲型病毒。重要的例子包括基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)、马亚罗病毒(MAYV)、委内瑞拉马脑炎病毒(VEEV)、罗斯河病毒(RRV)、辛德毕斯病毒(SINV)和森林脑炎病毒(SFV)等。尽管这些病毒对全球公共卫生有重大影响,表现为新的基孔肯雅病毒风险、高发病率以及经常导致严重或潜在致命的临床表现,但针对大多数甲型病毒感染的有效和特异性治疗选择,包括抗病毒药物和治疗手段,仍然有限。这代表了重要的公共卫生脆弱性,尤其是在热带和亚热带地区。为了解决这一令人担忧的情况,全面理解甲型病毒与其宿主之间的复杂相互作用对于识别病毒致病性决定因素以及相关疾病严重程度的因素至关重要。在此背景下,转录组学和基因表达分析方法已成为研究宿主对病毒感染反应的重要工具。这些方法提供了高分辨率的信息,揭示甲型病毒感染期间宿主基因表达的变化,有助于阐明疾病发病机制的分子机制。它们还可以提供关于识别生物标志物和分子特征、特定基因的上调或下调以及炎症、氧化、免疫和其他与感染相关的生物通路调控的重要见解。因此,本综述旨在通过基因表达分析方法,系统地综合研究甲型病毒与宿主相互作用的现有研究。将考虑使用RNA测序(RNA-seq)、单细胞RNA测序(scRNA-seq)、微阵列、逆转录定量PCR(RT-qPCR)和其他相关基因表达技术评估宿主基因表达的研究,涵盖不同宿主物种、组织、实验模型和感染条件。特别强调的是研究甲型病毒如何调控关键致病通路、炎症、组织特异性损伤以及其他与感染相关的生物过程。通过整合宿主基因表达谱的证据,本综述旨在突出与甲型病毒感染相关的重大转录变化和生物通路。这种整合可能提供关于病毒与宿主相互作用的见解,并支持识别潜在的分子治疗靶点、早期诊断工具和有效的预防策略。因此,本研究的总体目标是整合现有证据,研究甲型病毒感染期间宿主基因表达的调控,以阐明病毒与宿主的相互作用、与疾病相关的分子机制以及这些过程中的潜在关键因素。具体目标包括:描述甲型病毒感染的现状,为这些病毒提供临床和流行病学背景;描述宿主对甲型病毒感染的转录反应,识别不同甲型病毒和宿主系统中激活或抑制的分子机制的相似性和差异性;通过整合差异表达基因(DEGs)和富集的生物通路,描述与甲型病毒发病机制及其他生物过程相关的分子机制;绘制与甲型病毒感染不同阶段和过程相关的相关基因和生物通路,涵盖不同的实验系统,包括体外、体内和公开的转录组数据集;识别与甲型病毒-宿主相互作用相关的关键基因和分子因素,并探索其作为治疗靶点的潜力;识别现有文献中关于甲型病毒相关宿主基因表达的知识空白、重复模式和异质性来源。通过这种整合方法,综述预计能够产生足够的证据,支持关于治疗干预的假设和未来研究,包括对特定宿主基因进行操纵、编辑或沉默,这些基因的调控或抑制可能影响病毒复制,同时保持宿主细胞或宿主整体的存活。关键词:甲型病毒;宿主-病毒反应;转录组学;分子机制;差异基因表达;病毒发病机制

news.content: EPAPER LIVE TV DAWNNEWS URDU Images Herald Aurora CityFM89 Advertise Events Supplements Careers Obituaries Dawn E-Paper | September 15, 2026 Home Latest Violations Tracker Pakistan Opinion Business Images Prism World Sport Breathe Magazines Tech Videos Popular Archive Flood Donations Home Latest Violations Tracker Pakistan Opinion Business Images Prism World Sport Breathe Magazines Tech Videos Popular Archive Flood Donations Search Search Subscribe to notifications Get the latest news and updates from Dawn Not Now Allow Notifications Nowshera chikungunya outbreak local virus transmission, claim officials Ashfaq Yusufzai Published September 10, 2026 Email Your Name* Recipient Email* Cancel 0 In this file photo, an Aedes aegypti mosquito with the dengue-blocking Wolbachia bacteria is seen at a laboratory in the Wolbito do Brasil plant in Curitiba, Parana state, Brazil on September 1, 2025. — Reuters/File comments Join our Whatsapp Channel Add Dawn as a trusted source PESHAWAR: Officials of the health department have called the outbreak of chikungunya in Nowshera district a local transmission of the virus and stressed the need for immediate household vector control and contact tracing activities in the neighbourhoods of the areas that reported positive cases of the mosquito-borne disease. Officials in the department told Dawn that after the detection of 14 chikungunya cases in Nowshera and one in Malakand during the last one week, there was an urgent need to strengthen surveillance along with public awareness to prevent mosquito bites to control the spread of the infection. They said the chikungunya outbreak started in a union council of Kaka Sahib locality in Nowshera district on August 31 represented a credible, localised transmission warranting urgent, coordinated action from the district health authorities. “This chikungunya positivity rate and clustering pattern indicate a credible localised transmission signal warranting an immediate, coordinated public-health response,” an official told Dawn. They call for stronger surveillance, public awareness Officials said the chikungunya cases were reported in Nowshera and Malakand between August 31 and Sept 8. They said out of a total of 28 suspected cases, including 15 women and 13 men, 15 tested positive for the viral disease. The officials said that the chikungunya positivity rate remained 53.6pc, with the age of suspected cases ranging from five to 76 years. They said 10 of the 15 positive cases (67 per cent) aged 30 or below, indicating the outbreak was affecting children and working-age adults instead of being confined to older age groups. The officials said women totalled 53.6 per cent of those tested for the disease. They said the positivity rate was slightly higher among men (61.5 per cent) than women. The officials said a smaller cluster of three people was tested in Malakand, with one, a 12-year-old girl, testing positive for the viral infection. They said a smaller positive cluster was also identified in the area, warranting monitoring to prevent further spread of chikungunya. An advisory issued by the health department has outlined protective measures against chikungunya, including prevention of mosquito bites, the use of mosquito repellents on exposed skin, especially during daytime hours when Aedes mosquitoes are most active, and the wearing of long-sleeve shirts and long trousers, particularly for children and outdoor workers in the affected catchment. It said the people in endemic areas should take rest or sleep under mosquito nets, which should also be used by infants and young children during daytime naps. It called for the installation of window and door screens and keeping them in good repair to prevent entry to mosquitoes. The health department also said local health authorities should track treatment and recovery outcomes and re-testing where it was clinically indicated for confirmed chikungunya cases. news.content_original: EPAPER LIVE TV DAWNNEWS URDU Images Herald Aurora CityFM89 Advertise Events Supplements Careers Obituaries Dawn E-Paper | September 15, 2026 Home Latest Violations Tracker Pakistan Opinion Business Images Prism World Sport Breathe Magazines Tech Videos Popular Archive Flood Donations Home Latest Violations Tracker Pakistan Opinion Business Images Prism World Sport Breathe Magazines Tech Videos Popular Archive Flood Donations Search Search Subscribe to notifications Get the latest news and updates from Dawn Not Now Allow Notifications Nowshera chikungunya outbreak local virus transmission, claim officials Ashfaq Yusufzai Published September 10, 2026 Email Your Name* Recipient Email* Cancel 0 In this file photo, an Aedes aegypti mosquito with the dengue-blocking Wolbachia bacteria is seen at a laboratory in the Wolbito do Brasil plant in Curitiba, Parana state, Brazil on September 1, 2025. — Reuters/File comments Join our Whatsapp Channel Add Dawn as a trusted source PESHAWAR: Officials of the health department have called the outbreak of chikungunya in Nowshera district a local transmission of the virus and stressed the need for immediate household vector control and contact tracing activities in the neighbourhoods of the areas that reported positive cases of the mosquito-borne disease. Officials in the department told Dawn that after the detection of 14 chikungunya cases in Nowshera and one in Malakand during the last one week, there was an urgent need to strengthen surveillance along with public awareness to prevent mosquito bites to control the spread of the infection. They said the chikungunya outbreak started in a union council of Kaka Sahib locality in Nowshera district on August 31 represented a credible, localised transmission warranting urgent, coordinated action from the district health authorities. “This chikungunya positivity rate and clustering pattern indicate a credible localised transmission signal warranting an immediate, coordinated public-health response,” an official told Dawn. They call for stronger surveillance, public awareness Officials said the chikungunya cases were reported in Nowshera and Malakand between August 31 and Sept 8. They said out of a total of 28 suspected cases, including 15 women and 13 men, 15 tested positive for the viral disease. The officials said that the chikungunya positivity rate remained 53.6pc, with the age of suspected cases ranging from five to 76 years. They said 10 of the 15 positive cases (67 per cent) aged 30 or below, indicating the outbreak was affecting children and working-age adults instead of being confined to older age groups. The officials said women totalled 53.6 per cent of those tested for the disease. They said the positivity rate was slightly higher among men (61.5 per cent) than women. The officials said a smaller cluster of three people was tested in Malakand, with one, a 12-year-old girl, testing positive for the viral infection. They said a smaller positive cluster was also identified in the area, warranting monitoring to prevent further spread of chikungunya. An advisory issued by the health department has outlined protective measures against chikungunya, including prevention of mosquito bites, the use of mosquito repellents on exposed skin, especially during daytime hours when Aedes mosquitoes are most active, and the wearing of long-sleeve shirts and long trousers, particularly for children and outdoor workers in the affected catchment. It said the people in endemic areas should take rest or sleep under mosquito nets, which should also be used by infants and young children during daytime naps. It called for the installation of window and door screens and keeping them in good repair to prevent entry to mosquitoes. The health department also said local health authorities should track treatment and recovery outcomes and re-testing where it was clinically indicated for confirmed chikungunya cases. Conditions Chikungunya Cases in US Travelers Reach 89 with No Local Spread as Six Countries Carry Outbreak Notices Published Sep 10, 2026 3:25 AM EDT By Elena Vega ROSLAN RAHMAN | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket Eighty nine Americans have been diagnosed with chikungunya after returning from trips abroad this year, and not one of them caught it at home. Federal surveillance data current through August 11 show 89 travel-associated cases reported to the national arbovirus system from US states, plus one in a US territory, and zero locally acquired cases anywhere in the country. That combination is the whole story. The virus keeps arriving in the United States inside returning travelers, and so far this year it has not established itself in local mosquito populations the way dengue has in parts of Florida. The pattern shifts the risk from a neighborhood question to a trip planning question. For families, the practical consequence is narrow but real. Anyone booking travel to the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, Southeast Asia, parts of Africa, or several Indian Ocean islands is making a decision about mosquito precautions and, in some cases, vaccination. Anyone returning with fever and severe joint pain needs to tell a clinician where they have been. A Mosquito Illness Arriving by Airplane, Not by Backyard Chikungunya became a nationally notifiable condition in 2015, and the counts since then have swung with international outbreak cycles. Federal figures show 33 travel associated cases in US states in 2020, 152 in 2023, 241 in 2024 and 628 in 2025. Against that trend line, the current figures are preliminary and incomplete rather than reassuring. Arbovirus reporting lags because cases move from clinician to laboratory to state health department to the federal system, and the published national total is a snapshot that trails what states are seeing. The agency's areas at risk page, updated in early September, lists active outbreak notices for Bolivia, specifically the Santa Cruz and Cochabamba departments, along with northwest Costa Rica, French Guiana, Mauritius, Nicaragua and Suriname. A separate list flags ten countries where US travelers face elevated exposure even without a declared outbreak: Brazil, Colombia, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Peru, the Philippines and Thailand. Countries reach that list by producing a median of at least one case a year in US travelers over five years. Two locally acquired cases were reported in US states in 2025, in Florida and New York, the first since a single Texas case in 2015. None have been reported so far this year. Florida's Own Count Shows Where the Cases Land State surveillance offers a sharper local picture than the national total, though the two should not be added together. Federal tallies count cases by the patient's state of residence, while Florida maps them by county of exposure, and the two systems use different reporting cutoffs. Florida's weekly arbovirus surveillance report for the week ending August 29 counted 55 travel associated chikungunya cases with onset this year. Miami-Dade County accounted for 29 of them and Hillsborough for eight, with the rest scattered across eleven other counties. The same report recorded no locally acquired chikungunya cases in the state, alongside 73 locally acquired dengue cases in five counties. The countries of origin are the most useful detail in that report, and they do not match the federal risk lists. Forty of Florida's 55 cases were acquired in Cuba, which carries neither an outbreak notice nor a place on the elevated risk list. Nicaragua accounted for eight. That gap is a reminder that outbreak notices reflect what agencies have confirmed and prioritized, not a complete map of where the virus is circulating. The geography is not accidental. Florida combines heavy travel volume to the Caribbean and Latin America with a resident population that has family ties across the region, and it runs one of the most detailed mosquito surveillance programs in the country. Both species capable of transmitting the virus, Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, are established across the southern United States, and a returning traveler bitten during the viremic phase is how a travel case becomes a local one. Joint Pain That Can Outlast the Fever Most people infected with chikungunya develop symptoms, which distinguishes it from several other mosquito-borne viruses. Illness typically begins with sudden fever and severe joint pain, often in the hands and feet, and can include headache, muscle pain, joint swelling, and rash. Those typical symptoms overlap heavily with dengue, which is why travel history matters at the point of diagnosis. The acute phase usually lasts about a week. The joint pain does not always follow that schedule. A meaningful share of patients report arthritis like pain persisting for months, and older adults and people with existing joint disease tend to have the harder recoveries. Deaths are rare. Newborns infected around the time of delivery, adults aged 65 and older, and people with heart disease, diabetes or high blood pressure face the highest risk of severe illness. There is no antiviral treatment. Care is supportive, focused on fluids, rest and pain control, and clinicians generally rule out dengue before recommending certain pain medicines because the two illnesses look similar early on. Anyone who develops fever within two weeks of returning from an affected area should contact a clinician and mention the travel history, since testing is not routine without it. Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, confusion, or difficulty breathing warrant urgent evaluation. Vaccination, Repellent and Pre-Trip Planning The federal position on chikungunya vaccines distinguishes between destinations. Vaccination "is recommended for travelers visiting an area with an outbreak." For countries with elevated risk but no declared outbreak, vaccination may be considered for travelers planning an extended stay. That framing means a two week beach trip and a six month work assignment are different decisions, and both belong in a pre travel consultation rather than a self assessment. Travel clinics can advise on eligibility, since vaccine recommendations differ by age and health status, and pregnancy is handled separately. Current travel health notices are worth checking close to departure, since the outbreak list changes. Mosquito precautions apply regardless of vaccination status. The species that spread this virus bite during daylight hours, which makes daytime repellent use, long sleeves, and air-conditioned or screened lodging more important than a bed net for most itineraries. Cost and access vary. Travel vaccines are often not covered by standard health insurance, and county health departments and university travel clinics frequently price consultations below private travel medicine practices. Readers without insurance can ask a local health department what it charges before booking elsewhere. What remains unknown is where the year finishes. Reporting lags mean the published total will rise, international outbreak activity is still evolving, and no one can yet say whether this year will produce another locally acquired case in a US state. news.title_zh: 美国旅行者基孔肯雅热病例达89例,无本地传播,六个国家发布暴发通知——医学日报
news.source_body_en: The article reports that as of September 10, 2026, 89 cases of chikungunya virus were diagnosed in US travelers, with no local spread in the country. The CDC notes that the virus has not established itself in local mosquito populations, unlike dengue in parts of Florida. Federal surveillance data through August 11 show these 89 cases, plus one in a US territory, with no locally acquired cases. The agency's areas at risk page lists active outbreak notices for Bolivia, northwest Costa Rica, French Guiana, Mauritius, Nicaragua, and Suriname. Additionally, ten countries with elevated exposure include Brazil, Colombia, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Peru, the Philippines, and Thailand. These countries are identified based on producing at least one case per year in US travelers over five years. The article highlights that the risk of chikungunya is tied to travel rather than local neighborhoods, and individuals returning with fever and severe joint pain should inform clinicians of their travel history. The data are preliminary and incomplete, with arbovirus reporting lagging due to the multi-step process from clinicians to federal systems.
news.content_zh: 文章报道,截至2026年9月10日,美国旅行者中共诊断出89例基孔肯雅热病例,国内未出现本地传播。CDC指出,该病毒尚未在本地蚊群中建立起来,与佛罗里达部分地区登革热的情况不同。截至2026年8月11日,联邦监测数据显示,这些89例病例加上一个美国领土上的病例,均无本地感染病例。该机构的风险区域页面列出了玻利维亚、西北哥斯达黎加、法属圭亚那、毛里求斯、尼加拉瓜和苏里南的活跃暴发通知。此外,包括巴西、哥伦比亚、印度、印度尼西亚、墨西哥、尼日利亚、巴基斯坦、秘鲁、菲律宾和泰国在内的十个国家因每年至少产生一例美国旅行者病例而被列为高风险地区。文章强调,基孔肯雅热的风险与旅行有关,而非本地社区,返回时发热和关节痛的个人应告知医生其旅行史。数据初步且不完整,由于从临床医生到联邦系统的多步骤过程,虫媒病毒报告滞后。发布的全国总数滞后于各州所见情况。

What Anthropic’s latest report reveals AI researchers think that AI companies need more oversight on decisions about their AI models when deciding what part of artificial intelligence capabilities they want to restrict Nitin SJ Asariparambil Published: September 11, 2026 11:53 AM IST 3 minute Read Share × Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Reddit Comments Link Copied Highlights Anthropic has detected "threat actors" attempting to use its AI models for biological weapons research, including work on the chikungunya virus and bird flu Attempts to misuse Anthropic's AI involved evading regional blocks and using anonymising services to hide content and user identities The AI firm has implemented stronger safeguards in its latest models to restrict access to dual-use biological research queries Representative image "It has long been a concern that AI models might one day reach the level of capability where they can help to make existing pathogens more dangerous—or create entirely new ones," Claude maker Anthropic recently said. This was part of the AI firm's recent announcement of how it blocked efforts by certain "threat actors" who wanted to use its artificial intelligence models for a slew of questionable activities, including cyberattacks, surveillance, and, more dangerously, research on biological weapons. According to Anthropic, AI models getting more powerful means that cyberattacks no longer need sophisticated hacking skills. Even a single person with enough computing power can create cybersecurity threats that were not possible a year ago, Anthropic said. The company said it has added stronger safeguards in its latest models to restrict biological research that could also be used to make weapons. Therefore, "out of an abundance of caution", the AI firm said that its latest models, such as Claude Fable 5, have "stronger safeguards that restrict access to a wide range of dual-use biological research queries". However, it did state: "To our knowledge, no private company, AI or otherwise, has yet shared evidence of the potential misuse of their platforms for biological weapons development publicly." One such attempt involved "research that genetically alters an organism to create a new or enhanced biological property" on the chikungunya virus, it said. It is not merely the research that triggered the red flag. It was who triggered it. Anthropic explained: "The countries conducting this research are in regions where Anthropic does not supply service, so the platform tunnelled traffic through US infrastructure to evade our regional blocks, and used a zero data retention (ZDR) service to hide content. The developers of this platform used Claude through grey market resellers and synthetic accounts outside the ZDR channel to support their work, and explicitly referred to academic researchers as customers who were sensitive to the blocking actions of our safety classifiers." Another case involved research on highly pathogenic avian influenza, or bird flu. "The researcher in question accessed Claude from an unsupported region via US virtual private server infrastructure, using a privacy-email provider with an auto-generated username," it explained. And another case involved someone using an account "created from a randomly generated email address shortly before use and operated through anonymising US infrastructure, with operator logins traced to proxies shared with a banned account farm" who looked for access to "high-containment facilities and planned work with live orthopoxviruses". Variola, the agent of smallpox and Mpox, is an orthopoxvirus. This was Anthropic's third such report since March that detailed the misuse of AI. "The cases we share here aren't typical misuse, but rather examples of the most notable and novel threat activity we've identified to date," it stressed. The timing of the report, however, is highly suspect, according to AI ethics watchers. Two days before its publication, one of Anthropic's researchers announced that he resigned after alleging that the AI firm and its peers were not acting responsibly with AI development. He also detailed how the technology had the potential to eventually evade human control. Adding to that is how generative AI models are somehow individualised in commonspeak. "It is always Claude did this, ChatGPT did that. We often forget that there are big corporations run by people who benefit from their use. They need to be responsible for it," stated 37-year-old Kishan R, an AI researcher based in Noida. "It is instances like this where we need to explore the ethics of it. How are companies like Anthropic and xAI determining what constitutes safe use of their AI models? This is a democratic question and not a corporate one. Such rules should be determined by a regulatory body with oversight and powers," the researcher added. analysis_en.event: The developers of this platform used Claude through grey market resellers and synthetic accounts outside the ZDR channel to support their work, and explicitly referred to academic researchers as customers who were sensitive to the blocking actions of our safety classifiers." Another case involved research on highly pathogenic avian influenza, or bird flu.

supplementary_news.content: Home News Obituary Recipes Charity Special ಕನ್ನಡ Live TV RADIO Advertise Contact Us Matrimonial Properties Jobs General Ads Red Chillies Music Ask Dr Greetings Astrology Tribute Of Love Latest Chronic stress can disrupt cortisol, affect weight, sleep and blood sugar Mon, Sep 14 Bangladesh dengue crisis worsens: 52 deaths in September take total toll to 149 Mon, Sep 14 Faridabad hospital launches region’s first dedicated fever clinic Mon, Sep 14 Sirmaur: 4 test positive for H1N1 at Paonta Sahib hospital, shifted to isolation ward Mon, Sep 14 Bangladesh measles outbreak exposes major gaps in immunisation system Sun, Sep 13 Study reveals why virulent rabies infection overwhelms brain immunity Sun, Sep 13 Celiac disease increasingly detected among adults and elderly at PGIMS Sun, Sep 13 Health Dengue, chikungunya cases rise in Pune amid humid weather Wed, Sep 09 2026 08:43:20 AM Daijiworld Media Network - Pune Pune, Sep 9: Vector-borne diseases, including dengue and chikungunya, have been on the rise in Pune over the past few weeks amid hot and humid weather, leading to an increase in hospital admissions and prompting civic authorities to intensify action against mosquito breeding sites. Doctors have warned people against ignoring persistent fever, saying some dengue patients tend to delay seeking medical attention because the fever may temporarily subside during the day before returning in the evening. A doctor at a leading city hospital said some patients were reporting for treatment and admission only after suffering from fever for several days. “The fever in dengue patients gives confusing signals in the initial phase, as it often subsides during the day and intensifies in the evening. Some patients may feel they are recovering, but that is a dangerous misconception,” the doctor said. Dr Dattatraya B Patil, consultant physician at Noble Hospitals and Research Centre, said there had been a rise in viral fever cases in the hospital's outpatient department. “There has been a rise in the number of viral fever cases in our OPD. About 15–20% of these patients are testing positive for dengue. Patients should not ignore symptoms such as high-grade fever, eyeball pain, headaches, body and joint pain, vomiting, and loose motions. Dengue requires urgent attention; however, with proper medication and early treatment, it can be managed effectively,” he said. Several severe cases requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission have also been reported recently. Infectious diseases expert Dr Sujata Rege said hospitalisations due to dengue and dengue-like fever had increased, although such a trend was common during the monsoon. “While there is a rise in hospitalisations due to dengue and dengue-like fevers, this is a common trend every monsoon. Patients with a prior history of dengue may experience a faster drop in platelet counts than those infected for the first time. However, the treatment remains the same regardless of the strain,” she said. According to Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) assistant health officer Dr Rajesh Dighe, the civic body does not independently investigate the dengue strains circulating in the city as it requires specialised infrastructure. “We collaborate with the National Institute of Virology for this purpose, though the reports we receive typically only indicate whether samples are positive or negative for dengue,” he said. As of September 7, Pune had recorded 1,266 suspected dengue cases and 47 laboratory-confirmed cases, while 21 chikungunya cases had also been reported, according to PMC data. The number of suspected dengue cases has risen sharply since the monsoon. Pune recorded 175 suspected cases in June, 323 in July and 484 in August, with another 111 suspected cases reported during the first seven days of September. The civic body has also intensified its crackdown on mosquito breeding sites. More than 2,200 notices have been issued and fines exceeding Rs 4 lakh collected, Dr Dighe said. Other reports put the number of notices at 2,231 and the total fine at around Rs 4.04 lakh. Meanwhile, the Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) has inspected approximately 4.37 lakh homes, identifying mosquito breeding sites at around 3,900 locations. The civic body issued notices to 2,838 individuals and collected fines totalling more than Rs 10 lakh. Pimpri Chinchwad has so far recorded 16 confirmed and 684 suspected dengue cases, according to the latest figures. The civic action comes amid concerns over stagnant water left behind by intermittent monsoon showers, which has created favourable conditions for mosquito breeding. PMC has intensified anti-larval measures, fogging and containment activities around the homes of patients testing positive for dengue and chikungunya. At a recent meeting chaired by additional municipal commissioner Pavneet Kaur, the PMC announced a “Stop Dengue” campaign and directed all civic departments to contribute to mosquito-control efforts. Kaur said the health department would identify and destroy mosquito breeding sites, while the encroachment department would ensure that rainwater did not accumulate in materials seized during anti-encroachment drives. The encroachment department has also been asked to act against businesses conducting unauthorised tyre and puncture-related activities on roads and footpaths, where stagnant water can provide breeding grounds for mosquitoes. The solid waste management department has been directed to remove unusable materials from public spaces and create awareness about proper garbage collection and precautions against mosquito-borne diseases. Civic officials have urged residents to ensure that water does not remain stagnant in and around homes, offices and other premises, as even small quantities of stagnant water can become breeding sites for mosquitoes. supplementary_news.content: Search SF Sep 15, 2026 · 1:05 AM 215 Users OnlineOnline US| INTERNATIONAL| ASIA| Discussions Community💬 SF Startup Fortune Search ⌕ Home News AI Entrepreneur Interviews Guides Tech Opinion Latest Community Most Read Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google All... ShinyHunters Leaked Epstein's DMV File After... Oracle Plans More Layoffs in September... AI Wiped Out Kenya's College Essay... Home › Ai Anthropic Says It Blocked Scientists Using Claude for Bioweapons Research Anthropic disclosed five cases where researchers tried to use Claude for research that could aid biological weapons development, including a May 2026 attempt tied to a military institute studying the chikungunya virus. The same September 2026 threat report details a Russian state-linked hacking operation against Ukraine and drone-swarm software built with Claude Code. Elroy Fernandes Sep 10, 2026 · 9:01 PM · 5 min read · 1.4K reads Anthropic says it caught researchers using Claude in work that could support biological weapons, and the strongest part of the report is not the warning. It's the detail. Anthropic's September 10, 2026 threat report is not a vague safety memo. It names five biological misuse cases between December 2025 and August 2026, including one May 2026 request for help writing a grant application tied to gain-of-function work on chikungunya virus. According to Anthropic, the grant sought to identify mutations that could make the mosquito-borne virus more harmful as it passed through live animals, and the work was intended for a military research institute even though the researchers appeared civilian. That's the case making headlines. It should. Chikungunya can cause fever and severe joint pain that lasts for weeks or months, and Anthropic says there is no licensed therapeutic. A natural outbreak and a deliberate release could also be hard to tell apart, because the virus already circulates in the world. You don't need a Hollywood plot for this to be dangerous. You need a real lab and a plausible grant - and a model willing to help in the wrong place. Anthropic says its biological safety classifier blocked the grant-writing request. The story did not end there. Its investigators found that the traffic would normally have gone through an LLM platform serving dozens of life-sciences researchers, many of them virologists connected to civilian and military institutions. The platform tunneled traffic through US infrastructure to dodge Anthropic's regional blocks, used a zero-data-retention service to hide content, and later routed sensitive prompts that Claude refused to another model with weaker safeguards. That is the real shape of the problem. It is not one scientist asking one bad question. This Week in AI: Robots Take a Punch, Assistants Get Long-Term Memory, and Models Keep Getting Cheaper A dense week across robotics, model releases and AI research: humanoid robots duke it out, ChatGPT gets long-term memory, and frontier-adjacent AI keeps getting cheaper and faster. - how to build robots that handle physical impacts - AI models getting cheaper and more accessible features The same biological section also describes a researcher outside the US who spent weeks using Claude on avian influenza work involving mammalian adaptation and airborne transmissibility. In that case, Anthropic says its classifiers confined the exchanges to its weakest model class, Claude Sonnet 4 and Haiku 4.5, which limited the help the researcher could get. The company also found an orthopoxvirus grant application drafted on Opus 5 in about an hour, plus two cases involving venom peptides and toxin redesign. Some of this work could support vaccines or medicine. Some of it could also help make pathogens or toxins more dangerous. Here's the thing: in biology, those two paths often use the same methods. Claude is showing up in more than biology The report covers seven harm areas: cyber operations, influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud, biological misuse, conventional weapons development, and illicit distillation. The cyber section is the most concrete. Anthropic attributes one operation, GTG-20006, to an actor whose activity is consistent with public reporting on Midnight Blizzard. The group targeted Ukrainian and European government, military, diplomatic, defense and intelligence organizations, with drone technology and supply chains appearing again and again in the target set. Anthropic says GTG-20006 used AI-driven workflows for reconnaissance, phishing infrastructure, persistence, command and control, and data exfiltration. The report says the actor scanned more than two dozen Ukrainian government organizations, bulk-exported mailboxes from at least two drone component makers, targeted a military drone maker, and stole a software development kit for a drone vision system. Barely any humans touched some parts of the workflow. Separately, Anthropic says likely Russia-based freelance actors used Claude Code to build software for a full-stack autonomous first-person-view kamikaze drone swarm called DronDoc or Serafim. The system included shared swarm memory, terminal guidance, onboard attack and return-to-base behavior, and low-level chip logic. The report says the onboard model could select targets, including a "person" class, and issue detonation commands without a human in the loop. That line should stop you cold. Anthropic also says it disrupted six conventional-weapons cases: three in China, two in Russia - one in Yemen. The Yemen case involved guidance, navigation and control software for rockets and missiles, including a guided rocket that was test-fired and apparently failed. Chinese and Iranian government-aligned actors used Claude for surveillance work against diaspora communities and dissidents abroad, including Uyghur, Tibetan, Falun Gong, Iranian opposition and Jewish diaspora targets. That has nothing to do with innovation. It has everything to do with repression. The disclosure has a commercial edge This is not Anthropic's first threat report. The company published earlier reports in March, August and November 2025, including disclosures on a large-scale extortion operation using Claude Code, a North Korean employment fraud scheme, and a Chinese state-sponsored campaign abusing Claude Code. Four reports in 18 months is a pattern. That pattern cuts two ways. Anthropic is doing something most frontier labs still don't do with this level of specificity, naming viruses, military research settings, drone software, target classes and even internal threat-group labels. At the same time, Anthropic sells Claude to governments and companies that want proof its safety systems work. Frankly, both things can be true. The company has a commercial reason to look responsible, and its report still gives defenders details they would not have had otherwise. A New Trick Lets Anthropic Read Claude's Inner Thoughts Before It Speaks Anthropic says it has found a hidden 'workspace' inside Claude where the model quietly registers suspicions, including that it's being tested for blackmail, without ever saying so out loud. The July 6 research, built on a new open-sourced tool called the Jacobian lens, found Claude showed this kind of silent evaluation awareness in up to 26% of... - how to interpret Claude's internal thoughts - Claude model interpretability testing methods The harder question is scale. Anthropic can tell you what it caught. It can't tell you what every other lab missed, or what slipped through its own systems before the classifiers improved. That is why this report matters beyond Claude. If frontier models can now help with cyber operations, weapons software and dual-use biology, then safety monitoring is no longer a nice line in a policy document. It is part of the product.
